title: Fantastic stuff, but did make my skin dry after months of use...
text:
Let me start this by saying that I was initially drawn to this product because of its lack of harsh and excessive chemicals - any product that can work it's magic with only 5 ingredients is A-OK in my book, as we are constantly trying to limit our use of chemicals in general. I've now gone through two bottles of this stuff, and overall I've had success with it. I began using it in early December, and I'm more than halfway through the second bottle now, 4 months later. I'm 34, have very nice blemish-free skin, but did have some fine lines on my forehead and little crows feet, as well as two noticeable melasmas (dark spots) on my face. The first time I used this serum I immediately enjoyed the smooth silky application and how quickly my skin absorbed it. It leaves your face feeling a little "tight" after it dries, but I always followed it up with my moisturizer which took care of that.

I used it almost religiously, every morning and every night. After about a week, I started noticing my dark spots appeared a little lighter and less noticeable, and easier to cover up with makeup! I wasn't sure if it was my optimistic mind playing tricks on me, but it was very motivating to continue using it as directed. After 2 months of use and going through one full bottle, I can definitely say that this serum lightened my dark spots, smoothed my tiny wrinkles a bit, and overall gave my skin a plumpness and glow that only made me look more youthful.

So I ordered my second bottle, and after the third month, I started to have a reaction to it. I'm not sure if the product formula changed, or if that was just how long it took my skin to have repeated exposure to it before having a reaction. My experience was that it began drying my skin out, almost to the point of creating a dry skin/scaling effect on the surface of the skin. Having that dryness prompted me to exfoliate more, which in turn would leave little tiny "scabs" if you will, while the skin recovered. This is not cute, and does not work with my makeup. I stopped using it, and after about a week, it started clearing up. It's very disappointing, because I do really like this stuff and do think it works. After my wedding in 2 months, I am planning on working this back into my regimen in varying doses and frequencies, to see if I can find a way to continue using it without having that reaction. I will update my review with any further findings at that point.

title: Works great for nail art!
text:
I use this liquid latex as a barrier product for my nails. The shipment came a day early, even though I have prime and ordered on a weekend! Eventhough this is a rather small bottle, only about a half ounce, it will last me quite a while for the purpose I am using it. My favorite thing about this product and the reason I bought the Graftobian brand is because it has a small brush in the lid, super convenient!!! This means that I don't have to use on of my nail are brushes, and then attempt to get the dried latex out of it later. I have included a few photos of how I use the latex, but here is a quick rundown:
- Paint around the cuticle and nail, the latex paints on white, but will dry clear. You only need a thin layer. Also, even once the latex is completely dry, it will still feel "tacky".
- Paint nails as usual, then peel the latex off while polish is still wet, starting at the base of the nail bed and peeling towards the tip of the nail (sometimes a pair of tweezers is helpful for this). The latex should peel off all in one piece.
- Clean up any remaining polish with a stiff angled brush and acetone, although this should be greatly decreased because of your latex :)
I really love this brand because it peels off nicely all in one piece, and I would absolutely recommend the Graftobian liquid latex to anyone looking for a quality brand to try!

title: I like it! Good buy.
text:
First of all, forget the "fogless" thing. No mirror is fogless; it's a fundamental quality of smooth surfaces that they will mist up when wet and in varying temperatures. The reason this mirror works is because of the rope and its light weight. The mirror is plastic, but reflects clearly and true. Hanging it on the included hook means that you can take t down and hold it under the water to equalize the temperature somewhat. This makes it less foggy, although water beads on it quickly. I use my shower squeegee to wipe it down every so often. The included "rope" is actually about 5 feet of nylon paracord, so it holds up well and shouldn't rot. It also has a plastic slide should you wish to cinch it up. A metal hook with a glue-tab back is included to hang the mirror on when you're not holding it.

Overall, it works as well as or better than any other shower mirror I've used. Again, it is NOT fogless, because fogless is an impossibility absent some high-tech coating or something. As a mirror, it works fine. Its best quality is that it's very light and easy to hold or hang around your neck. I like the fact that I can just hold it under my chin to see to shave my neck, and I don't have to crane my neck as I would with a wall-mount. Frankly I think the price is a tad high for what you get (I'd sooner have paid 10 bucks for metal or glass), but for what it is, it works well and I like it.

text:
I've always had very sensitive ears. I initially tried to pierce them when I was 15 and they quickly became infected. My mom could only wear 14 karat gold so I later tried that as well. I tried to pierce 3 different times over the years. I cleaned my piercing as directed. I applied the special solution the piercer gave me. I tried applying hydrogen peroxide all kinds of stuff and each time my ears became swollen and infected a little faster each time. Most recently I had to take my earings out after just 5 days.
I have a friend who's a jeweler and she explained to me that even 14 karat gold sometimes contains nickel. She recommended that I try titanium instead. So I did. At first it seemed like the solution but after a few weeks my ears were swollen again. I tried mixing salt and water at home to make something that other reviews are saying as the same thing as this product. It's not. My ears were still swollen. No home remedies seemed to be working so I ordered this product. The issue cleared up after only a few days. It's been a year now and my ears are still pierced. I haven't even applied this product in around 6 months. The nozzle is clogged and that seems to be a design flaw. The product itself has done wonders for me. I'd recommend this to anyone who has had trouble with ear infections. Also try piercing with titanium. Not all piercers seem to carry it but you can probably fine someone that will be willing to order some for you.

PROS

For the price, would strongly recommend as a daily use chair for relaxing after a hard day at work or after working out.

title: The Best Mineral Foundation.
text:
I have tried them all. Everyday Minerals, Bare Minerals, mall kiosk versions, etc. This one blows them all out of the water. For a more detailed review, keep reading.

I ordered this kit in Fair, but I have more like "Light" complexion in most foundations. This kit only comes in Fair or Medium for the lightest options so Fair was my best bet. I received the kit on time. I will break down my thoughts on each product for you:

Foundation in "Fair": A true neutral Fair shade. Light enough for my redhead sister, and maybe me in the dead of winter. The coverage is stellar and I need far less product to cover with this an any previously sampled mineral makeups.

Foundation in "Fair II": A warm, light color. Similar to the Bare Minerals shade "Fairly Light." Much better for my full face in the summer, but I'll still need a bit of bronzer to really balance it with my tan shoulders. Coverage is same, amazing coverage. The texture is silkier than other mineral products. I can't even feel it when applying. Also, the finish is somewhere between matte and dewy. So, so, so natural, even in pure daylight. I don't need a Snapchat filter. It really is a gorgeous finish. Not drying, like Everyday Minerals, not shiny like Bare Minerals. Not as gritty a texture as either. I just love it. Perfect for dry skin. Does not settle into crows feet or nasalobial creases. Does not oxidize.

Warmth: Necessary for a little change in the shad for me. I sweep he tiniest whisper of this stuff over my cheeks, nose, temples, and chin and one tiny dip will do the whole thing. Not orange, and not ruddy red.

Bisque: Holy. Something. Honestly, covers better than a lot of liquid concealer! Kind of light for me, so it's great as an undereye concealer and as a spot concealer BEFORE applying my Fair II shade all over. Doesn't budge after it sets.

Tan Eyeshadow: Pretty, sparkly, a nice everyday lid color. Very sheer. I could do without it, but it really is a nice addition to the kit considering the low cost.

Setting Veil: Not really necessary for me, since I tend to be dryer-skinned. I guess it would be nice for oily folks but I'm just not sure what I'll use it for.

Brush set: Eh. It's not going to change your life. It sheds a bit, it's not soft, but the eyeshadow brush is okay. Give them to makeup beginners like a niece or cousin. Cute little set in a red bag.

Overall, fantastic Foundation, Bisque, and Warmth. Considering how inexpensive this is, I don't mind the extra products included. From now on I may order individually or just order the kit again. One jar of mineral foundation at sephora costs more than all of these products together so... Give it a try!

Tip for us light skinned girls: Go with Fair kit if you are truly fair. However if you lean to light/medium or just "light" you may want to try the medium kit.

title: Brings desiccated curls back to life!
text:
I LOVE this shampoo and conditioner. As someone who thought she just had frizzy, not-quite-straight, not-quite-wavy, and generally unruly hair for decades, this shampoo and conditioner duo was a revelation. The moisturizing effects of this shampoo and conditioner brought the curls I thought I'd lost in childhood back to life! Using the conditioner as a once-weekly deep conditioning treatment means my hair stays curly and perfectly moisturized even in Chicago winters when the dry heat pumped into every building would otherwise desiccate my hair. FIRST-TIME USERS: Especially if you're used to washing and conditioning your hair every single day, I recommend easing into incorporating this shampoo and, in particular, conditioner into your routine. If your scalp is used to producing enough oil to replenish your hair after daily washing, it will likely take your scalp some time to adjust. Your hair may feel heavier for the first few weeks or so, but if you allow your hair and scalp time to adjust, your patience will be rewarded.
In accordance with best practices for curly hair, I recommend washing your hair no more frequently than every two or three days. If your hair isn't particularly dry, then condition just as often; no need to deep-condition. If your hair is particularly dry in winter, you can condition every day and deep-condition once a week, but only shampoo once or twice a week. A little goes a long way with this wonderfully effective duo!
I've tried other products before and after using R+co Atlantis moisturizing shampoo and conditioner, and I keep coming back to these products. Used as needed for your hair-type, these little bottles are worth every penny.

title: A Review of No-Mes Fingernail Clippers, American Made by Industrial Tool and Die Co. Inc.
text:
Today we are going to take a look at something a little bit different on the Soapbox. Usually we do Bible reviews and post Christian articles. We are going to look at No-Mes Fingernail clippers. I know, this is unusual, but I think it will be a good thing. I found myself looking for a replacement set of clippers. I had inherited a set of American made clippers from my Father. I keep them on my key ring as a functional memento. My Dad passed away a few years ago. He was a big fan of good tools and American craftsmanship. He used to fabricate his own tools when he was a mechanic. When I use them, I think about him. I wanted to get another pair of American made nail clippers to keep on my key chain so I could put my other ones up. I didn’t want to lose them. So, I set out to find an American made set of clippers.

I wanted American made clippers because I have had several Chinese made ones. They are dull, they smash the nail, they tear the nail, they break, and they cost too much for what they are. I know there are at least 8 sets of clippers sitting in drawers at my house unused, because they are garbage. As a Christian, I am opposed to communism. It is a godless system that forces the worship of the government and created things instead of God. Communism is not good for human flourishing. I grew up during the cold war and remember the horrors of communism reported to us on the nightly news. This was back when news was not yellow journalism, a term I fear the youth of this nation knows nothing about. My Dad and his brothers were all vets. My Uncle Larry was in the first class of Air Commandos. He flew three tours in Vietnam fighting communism. Before the Air Force he was a Marine. My Dad was in the Air Force and served in Northern Africa in between the Korean War and the Vietnam war.

I began looking for some clippers by doing a search on the internet for, “American made fingernail clippers.” This lead me to Amazon. I saw several pop up but only one was truly American made, the No-Mes clippers from Industrial Tool and Die Co. Inc. in Troy, New Jersey. I felt angry. I’m not going to lie. I was angry that much of our industry has been shut down and shipped out. Not just shipped out, but shipped out to communists who enslave their own people to make shoddy quality goods for us to buy at low prices. Then the anger turned to a fondness. Fondness for a company started by one man and kept in the family. I’ve never met anyone from Industrial Tool and Die Co. Inc. I’ve never talked with them outside of my e-mails. I know nothing about them other than what their site says. Just the fact that they are in America making a quality product, for a decent value, warmed my heart. When I went looking for them on the web, I was surprised to see that they didn’t have much of a web presence, so I decided I would e-mail them and ask them for some clippers to review. They graciously accepted and here we are. I hope to bring some recognition to them and their product.

The clippers arrived in a padded envelope. They were packed in a little white box with some padding and an instruction card with the warranty information on the other side. The clippers were in a little plastic bag. When I took them out, I noticed they were a bit larger than my old clippers. They also had a tool that was noticeably missing. The nail file/nail cleaner. I wondered why this was absent. After using the clippers it was obvious that a nail file was not needed. The clippers cut the nail cleanly leaving no burs or rough spots. You just don’t have any snags to file. I was pretty impressed by that. I noticed something these clippers had that most do not, is the bin that catches the clippings. No finding them later on the floor or seeing them snap and fly out into the room. The nails are cut cleanly, not smashed or torn. The blades are sharp and there were no irregularities on them to cause the clippers to malfunction. They simply, did what they were intended to do! Amazing! I know, a product that did what it is supposed to do… How could we demand such a thing? Kids, you don’t know what you are missing. When you grow up using substandard tools and equipment, then replacing them with more of the same when they break, you never get to know what it is like to work with something of quality. These clippers are just good quality clippers. They are not gimmicky at all. The bin works the way that it is supposed to. I noticed there isn’t much travel with the handle the way that it functions and it is easy to hold. They are a bit wider and have good flat spots for you to squeeze the handles. There are also grooves in the surfaces to help you keep hold of them. They were much easier to use than traditional styled clippers. Traditional styled clippers allow the handle to swing around 360 degrees. These do not. They won’t pop out from under your thumb the way others will. They also have a hole in the end so they can be kept on a key ring. The little metal flap that you fold over the bin is also the surface that the cam on the handle engages to actuate the clippers. It has two protrusions, one on each side. I think a person could use them to clean under a nail if they had to. These would make a great stocking stuffer, or gift for the man in your life. They are a good value as well. You can pick them up on Amazon for about $13. Here is the product description from the Amazon product page, “The patented no-post/no-swivel design offers a simpler no fumbling method of trimming nails. Clippings stay inside a specially designed compartment, unlike ordinary nail clippers that launch your nail clippings across the room. The "No-Mes" nail clipper is easily emptied by opening the handle, then folds up for compact storage. All hardened tool steel with precision ground cutting edges, polished and chrome plated finish. The "No-mes" nail clipper is designed and manufactured in the USA to last forever and is guaranteed for life!” ,I really appreciate having a good pair of nail clippers handy. Don’t be fooled by imitators or cheap Chinese made knock-offs. Make sure to get the No-Mes clippers. If only they could figure out a way to put a knife blade, laser beam, grappling hook, and internet on these… nope, just kidding. They are great the way they are.

title: Celiacs Beware
text:
This product is NOT gluten free.

I wanted to like this product. I really, really did. My primary reason for ordering it that it claims to be "fragrance free". I also read the label and was happy to see their wasn't wheat protein, considering that I'm also sensitive to gluten. Unfortunately though, there IS hidden gluten in this product. First off, the product has an extremely strong smell and therefore is not unscented. Second of all, I had a horrific reaction after using it where the skin on my scalp, face, neck, upper back, etc. became very inflamed and my lips and eyes swelled up. I knew it had to be gluten, but it doesn't list any on the label. So, I called the company. Turns out that their tocopherol on their ingredient list is derived from wheat. Who would know? Not me. No one, actually, since they do not clearly label that. Companies like this, especially companies who market to the sensitive/allergic population, need to know how DANGEROUS it is to include hidden allergens in their labels. Please mark your labels clearly, companies. Thank you.

title: For Mature Skin
text:
Don't you just hate it when you splurge on a foundation and toner because touted to slide *over* not *into* tiny lines in your face and instead of the airbrushed blanc mange you imagined, you see the product settling into and emphasizing wrinkles that before the makeup were invisible?
Argh! I know I'm not wasting time and money to look *older*.
Countess is the only makeup that doesn't accentuate lines and that does give older/dryer skin a flawless, dewy look.
That's the good...no the great.
There are a few hurdles with this makeup:
It's hard to find. It's never been sold in retail stores. This makes selecting the shade challenging.
Amazon has it, though it appears there are shortages, now, it seems, so stock up if you can
Also it's not cheap.
The toner runs about $60 and the foundation, $50. Though, a little goes a very long way so cost is deceptive (in a good way).
If you really want makeup that will not settle into the tiny lines of your face (making you look older), Countess is the only option.
Note, the toner and makeup *are* oil based (though very sheer), so probably not for younger women.

title: Currently Testing the product, Will Update in TWO WEEKS.
text:
Hello Amazoner's,

I just received this product and I am giving it 3 stars because I am just starting to use it (Day 2) and will update after 2 weeks of use with photos.
I love that the product is a "natural herbal' product. The "Licorice Extract" is the natural lightening agent. (via research)
I have used all of the following that contains hydroquinone which are:
Ambi Fade Cream
Nadinola
Dr. Fred Summit Bleach Cream
Black and White Bleach Cream
Porcelana.
Each of these creams contain hydroquinone.
I did my research of the pros and cons of the hydroquinone and some reviewers got great results, others not so lucky, like me.
After each use at different months of the year, I have noticed my hyperpigmentation just got red with burning sensations instead of lighter, so I discontinued the use due to my dermatologist orders. My derm did not recommend a prescription for my PIH (Post Inflammatory Hyperpigmentation) because it was strong and the pigmented area was on my face.
My hyperpigmentation is right on my face between my eyebrows so that is where the desperation to rid of the discoloration came to. I really wanted to get rid of it as soon as possible because that's the first thing I see when I look at my face in the mirror. It made me self-conscious. I don't like to wear a lot of makeup nor have the time to look flawless (MOM OF 3 toddlers) I had gotten this PIH due to an allergy from taking an NSAIDS medication which cause a rash on my face. My derm prescribed me hydrocortisone 2.5% to relieve the itching and inflammation.
After my itching went away, I was left with PIH. Hydrocortisone helped with the itching and inflammation, but not the PIH on top of that my derm said not to use the hydrocortisone over 2 weeks period because of the side effects of the skin thinning.
Knowing Hydroquinone was not the best idea for my skin, I decided to research some 'brightening/lightening" creams without hydroquinone.
I stumbled upon Aveeno positively radiant cleanser and the Tone Corrector with Vitamin A. Both seem to help a TAD, but not as fast as I would have hoped so I decided to try this Derma E Skin lighten cream.

SO FAR, what I can tell you is that the color is very light beige, no scent.
Looks creamy at a glance, but when applied it is a bit pasty upon drying after application
(Think of a very thin layer of dried toothpaste on the skin). (A little goes a long way)
It kinda seems like a concealer after it dries on my skin, the color is definitely a reason why it would appear "lighter"
No skin redness or irritation.
I know it will take some time to possibly see a difference.
Size is reasonable for its price at $6.47 (free shipping orders over $35)
I am Asian and 28 years old skin color is light. Think of a real lightskin Alicia Key's.
My skin is combo, but the current cold weather calls for frequent moisturizing (Michigan)
I will update with before and after photo's in 2 weeks time.
I will also be testing out the KOJIE SAN SOAP & whitening cream after I received it.

title: Not for the faint of feet
text:
Alright y'all, this ain't your basic foot rasp. If you have mild calluses, I really suggest you look elsewhere. However, if you, like me, basically have hooves for heels, then this may be you new holy grail of extraneous foot skin removal.

A word of warning -- this thing will take off the tips of your toes if you're not careful. I nicked my pinky toes twice before I figured out how to NOT do that. But injury aside, after I learned how to wield this mighty weapon, I've been unafraid to wear flip flops since. That's HUGE for me. I have nasty feet. NASTY. Calluses, fissures, you named it. I've had 'em all. And now they're all gone, thanks to this gigantic foot grater.

It's easy to use: take a shower, put a little liquid lotion (or shampoo or conditioner) on the rasp, apply to feet. Very little pressure is needed. You may need to try a few different angles so you don't accidentally grind off the skin you want to keep. This thing works quickly, so stop while you're ahead -- it's possible to, without even realizing it, work your way down to very delicate layers of skin that shouldn't be walked on.

So I hope you get the idea. Minor foot issues? Don't buy this. Scaly, nasty hobbit-feet? This is the cheese grater for you. It'll change your life. Or just your feet. Or both!

title: Exceeded My Expectations
text:
Okay, I'm old enough to remember the old Remington, and Norelco razor commercials. Now that's out of way, and with the perspective of the fact that I have owned at least a dozen different electric shavers in my lifetime, I was in the market for a new one. The one I had previous to this Panasonic was a Braun series 5...had it for 12 years because it came pretty close to matching the performance of a razor, and it was reliable. It's only short coming was with a 2-3 day growth, it bordered on painful to cut through it mostly because the replacement blades were much inferior to the original, and my face felt it!

I decided to see if there were any shavers out there were under $100, that could maybe replace my old workhorse Braun, and give me at least a little better results, and was wet/dry capable. The Panasonic fit the bill, and I decided to give it a try. When I got it and saw the massive shaving head I thought, I had made a mistake....that no way was this going to be able to get into those tough areas on the jaw line and on either side of the under the chin. Plus I was dreading that infamous "skin break in period" everyone talks about. My first shave was simply amazing....it got into the areas I was worried about without a whimper...and sailed through all the other areas like a rider mower through a 9' X 12' lawn...it cut my shaving time in half and the results were very impressive...and didn't irritate my skin one bit. So I decided to not shave for 3 days (I'm retired, so I can get away with that) and see how it handled this test. It hit the heaviest growth on my chin...the motor changed pitch slightly, but it cut through it...and without any pain....like it was a one day's growth. I had to make a few additional passes but what usually took me 5 mins to accomplish with my old Braun, only took 3 mins, with fantastic results. Let's be honest...no electric shaver can match a razor in closeness, but this Panasonic comes as close as I've ever seen, or felt. Throw in the bonus that you can wet shave, and run it under the faucet or shower to clean it out and you've got a real winner! Frankly, for the money...you'd be hard pressed to find a better electric shaver and the fact that it was under $100 makes it a real gem. The only thing lacking is that it doesn't come with a holder or stand....big deal, I stand it up in the corner of my vanity, and it does just fine. This shaver is a winner in price, performance, and convenience. Give it a shot.

title: Perfect for carrying foundation/etc on the go!
text:
As seasons change, I augment my foundation with oils, moisturizers and the like. Most mornings it would take 5 minutes mixing up the base, rosehip or jojoba oil, HA, mattifyling powder or whatever my skin felt like it needed. It was an annoying part of my routine and I couldn't really touch it up. Yeah, I could make some in a little jar, but it often got lost in my bag or even ended up opening from being tossed about.

Two of these and I'm set. Now I have one for summer (no oil added, but powder instead and a tinge darker because tanned skin) and winter (lighter shade with oils and HA added) This is wonderful for touch ups because you can just dab your finger on the sponge and pat on your skin. A Beauty Blender works great too. I'm super happy to see there's extra inserts as well. Not a necessary part of the compact, IMHO, but if you wanted to make several for easy swapping, the extra will help.

Unsure why people think it's a waste of product. My intent is to just remove the sponge when it's getting 'dry' and dab on my skin, then blend it out. No more waste than a traditional makeup sponge. You can squeeze the sponge until it's almost dry, so I don't think it will waste much.

The application pad included is thin and flimsy, but they all are. Toss it and use your fingers or favorite sponge.

I'm wondering if I can use my night oil blend in this for when I forget to put it on before bed...Guess I'll have to buy some more!

title: ABSOLUTELY LOVE IT!
text: I just bought this shampoo yesterday, after reading many good reviews about it.  My hair is in desperate need of help.  I'm 8 months pregnant and my hair has thinned out dramatically over the last six months or so.  My scalp has been very dry and itchy, which I understand are two major causes of hair loss in women (unhealthy scalp).  I have alternated shampoos many many times this past year just looking for something that will keep my scalp and hair healthy and moisturized.  Certain ones have worked okay at first use, but my hair is still thinning, and it eventually breaks, frizzes out, or get too oily after just a day or two without a wash, and daily combing and styling.  Anyway, I used the L'Oreal Paris EverStrong Thickening Shampoo for the first time last night.  I was able to see a very nice difference immediately!  When I say "immediately", I mean, while I was in the shower!  I was surprised that it lathered, for one.  I was under the impression that Sulfate-Free and Paraben-Free shampoos did not lather, but I'm kind of glad it did because I have naturally curly hair, so when I don't pack on conditioner, I have a real hard time combing out my hair after a shower.  I shampooed my hair and rinsed as usual, and my hair felt sooooo nice and smooth even under the water.  After applying conditioner and leaving it on for a few minutes, I rinsed it out and my hair felt even softer, and to be 100% honest, it even felt stronger.  The smell is something I was able to get past.  I mean, as I browsed their line at Target trying to decide which I really wanted (almost went for the Intense Nourishing Shampoo), I opted for the thickening since that is the biggest issue for me right now.  The only reason why I was hesitant about this one was due to the smell.  The others had really amazing scents, while this was VERY different.  Some people stated "medicinal" which is close, but I actually told my husband that it smells like something a man would use in the shower - very bold and well, manly.  After my shower, I towel dried my hair and was pleased at how super easy it was to comb out.  I wasn't standing there stroking my hair a million times to get the tangles out.  I braided my hair at night and was very happy with the way my hair looked and felt this morning.  It was obvious that my texture was better, and well it is too soon to see any difference as far as thickening goes, my hair does appear to have more volume after I straightened it this morning.  It's so soft and bouncy, and I did NOT need any styling products or anti-frizz or heat serums in my hair.  I have never used a shampoo that has made my hair feel the way it feels now - even after a salon visit.  Just the results I've had in one day alone has convinced me that this will from now on be my go-to shampoo, but in time I'm curious to see an improvement with the strength and thickening claims by this product.  OH!  And for the first time in FOREVER, my scalp doesn't itch like crazy.  So, I truly believe that in the mean time I will not experience any more hair loss based on how rejuvenated my scalp feels today.  Now lets see if I'll be back in the near future to update everyone on the strength, and improvement in thickness by this awesome product!

title: Not What I Expected
text:
I was hoping to be able to give this item a better review. I don't necessarily think it's a BAD product; I think it's just not right for me.
In my search for an aluminum-free deodorant that actually works, I came across this Nivea product. I've always like Nivea brand stuff and the reviews were overall good. So I ordered it.
My reasons for disappointment aren't huge, but a big enough deal for me that I won't be using this product again. The scent is WAY overpowering. It honestly reminds me of my Nana's bathroom. It's a sweet, powdery, really strong smell. Like Aquanet and Clinique lipstick and gardenia mixed together...or something of that nature. I say that because those are things I'd find in my Nana's bathroom. If you start to sweat (which most people generally do when they're working out, chasing their children around, doing heavy house-cleaning, or driving in ridiculous Denver traffic), the product kicks in--or I should say the product smell kicks in. I simply don't like feeling like I Febreezed my armpits.
Now, it may be aluminum-free, which of course is a much desired facet! However, it's also free of wetness protection. I don't sweat a lot but I feel like this deodorant made me sweat more. I've never had so much wetness underarm before. It made me very self-conscious.
Also, I've been to Germany. Two of my brothers even lived there for awhile. Many of the people we met didn't seem too concerned about their personal odor (no worries--it wasn't like it was in France), but I don't think adding the "Genuine Authentic German" part of the description is necessary or effective. People in Germany don't smell that awesome. So...what does that really have to do with effectiveness?
All in all, I wouldn't recommend this but I wouldn't NOT recommend it. I think there are elements to this deodorant that just didn't work for ME, but obviously worked for others. So...I leave this game of Russian Roulette in your hands, customer. God speed.

title: Great Quality - Great Price
text:
I love making and customizing skin care products for family and friends. I am making an eye cream for my sisters and friends for Christmas and thought these little jars would be perfect.
1. Yes they are plastic - a medium weight, nice quality plastic. I have purchased glass containers in the past, but they are not as cost effective as plastic and these will definitely travel better.
2. They are about 0.24 oz/7 grams - perfect for an eye cream or lip gloss. I could see using these as sample containers, but they are too small for anything other than an eye cream, lip balm, etc.
3. They do not have a weird chemical smell, not sure how else to explain it, but I have purchased plastic containers in the past that smell awful and even with multiple washings the smell does not seem to dissipate.
4. The tops did not cross thread, and I screwed them on and off several times just to be sure. They fit perfectly on the jars and did not leak when turned upside down. Very important because whatever gift I give my sister she is going to shake to try to figure out what it might be.
5. They are easily decorated, I used washi tape on the lid and a printed label on the body of the jar.
I will definitely be purchasing more of these as I can totally see making a lip gloss collection with them - I bought a bakery scents fragrance collection that will work perfectly as lip glosses. I highly recommend these little containers for all of the reasons listed above. Happy Creating!

title: So much bubbly fun!!
text:
I am always looking for a good mask for my sensitive skin. I have been using a mud mask but they tend to flake everywhere while they're drying. This carbonated mask looked super fun to use so I ordered it on a whim to get me up to the one day shipping threshold.
The mask comes with a small spatula under the lid and zero instructions in english, so I had to google to find out how to use it. You're supposed to apply a thick layer to unwashed skin and leave it to bubble completely, around 5 to 7 minutes. Then you can either rinse it off or rub it in, then rinse with lukewarm water.
The mask is somewhat stretchier than a normal clay mask- almost like a starchy pudding. I used the spatula to apply it, and made sure that I didn't leave the container open too long. I'm not sure if it's the oils or the air that causes the reaction so I made sure to avoid contaminating the jar with either.
I ended up leaving mine on for 8 minutes to get the full bubble effect, and then I tried to rinse. The bubbles came off easily but the underlying mask was harder to remove and kind of slimy. I ended up having to use a konjac sponge soaked in steaming water to get the mask off, but it came off easily with that combo. It took a LOT of rinsing to get the mask out of my sponge so make sure you use a backup one or a washcloth. My skin afterward looked super smooth and hydrated, so the work was worth it. I followed the rest of my routine and have had zero issues with this affecting my skin negatively.
Overall, this is a fun mask that I would recommend to anyone looking for a twist on a clay mask. I think that it would be a good idea to use this in the shower when I try it again next week, just so it's less messy.

title: Okay, but liquids might leak from bottles.
text: I bought this for an international trip to hold my different creams, lotions, and toners. The small jars and even some of the bottles held my shampoo and conditioners just fine. The bag was in my carry-on on my trip to Germany so it was definitely jostled around and in and out of my bag for security checks. I kept it upright as best as I could and still, the bottles that had liquids in them, slowly leaked all over the bag. By the time I unpacked it, a fourth of my toner had leaked from a larger bottle and my hair oil, in the smaller bottle, had left a thin coating on all the bottles and jars. If all of your toiletries are on the thicker side, they will be pretty secure. But I wouldn’t trust them for liquids again.

title: Thick Layer is Key
text:
I have seen some videos of painful removal of these black masks and was a little nervous to try. I have been having some really strange issues with my skin over the last several months and I really wanted a deep "cleaning" to see if that would help, so I bought this mask. My skin over the last several months has gone back and forth from breakouts to dryness and skin actually flaking off. When I wear makeup base, you can see my pores like foundation dots all over my cheeks. I have some breakouts around my nose and on my chin right there with the flaking skin - very odd!

Anyway, I applied the mask the first time in the really thin layer and it dried in about 20 minutes. I had a hard time pulling it off which I figured was because the mask was too thin. So, a few days later I tried again with a thicker layer that that was much easier to remove. I didn't have pain per say, but it was more like pulling off a Band-Aid or getting an eye brow wax - not really painful but, not painless either if that makes any sense.

After the first mask, I didn't feel like my skin was showing much improvement. It was softer and that was nice, but the following morning, I was flaky again. However, after the second time I used the mask, my skin was MUCH softer and in the two days since, my flaking is much improved. I am hopeful that using this mask on a regular basis will clear up this issue for good!

title: Love my CreaClip!!!!
text: So I have been cutting my own hair (trimming ends) for a little over a year now.  It really all comes down to the cost that these places charge you being so outrageous.  I understand stylists/hairdressers need to make money, but spending over $20 to get an inch or two trimmed off my ends every month is just not affordable to most people.  So I started cutting my own hair at home using the grooming shears I purchased to trim my dog's "grinch feet" and ears in-between grooming sessions.  They're sharp and get the job done, so why not share them? lol  Anyway, I have super curly hair so I usually cut my hair after a shower.  I part it, and try to cut as evenly across as possible.  I don't have to be perfect because when my hair dries it curls and if it is a little uneven nobody will be the wiser (unless I straighten it).  I watch Shark Tank and saw this product and immediately knew I had to have it.  I purchased it and the day it arrived it was time to put it to the test.  I already saw it domed on Shark Tank so I knew how to use it, but it did come with a little leaflet showing how to use the clips.  This must be a new addition because I've seen other reviewers unhappy that it came with no directions and you had to go to YouTube to figure out how to use it.  So they saw feedback, and adjusted to make customers happy.  Wonderful.  I personally have no need for the blue clip for bangs, but it came in a pack so I have it just in case a friend may need one in the future. Using the CreaClip is super easy: you brush your hair forward with your head down (getting out all tangles) and rest your chin on your chest.  Then you clip the CreaClip as close to the roots as possible, check to make sure the bubble is in the middle for an even cut, and slide down stopping at your desired length.  Then you can cut straight across, or vertically for a "textured" look.  It then advises you to clean with a toothbrush and shampoo after use and let it dry.  My hair didn't have any product in it since I just showered, so I ran it under the tap to get the little amount of hair that got trapped when I trimmed it out, and let it air dry.  It would have been great if it came with a little pouch or something to store them in, but it doesn't.  I keep mine in a ziplock bag, nothing too fancy.  I love this product, so glad I saw it on Shark Tank, and I love it.  It is so worth it to save money cutting your hair at home.  I mean, we dye our hair at home, why not cut it as well and save tons of money?!?!?! I would definitely recommend this to anybody looking for a cheap alternative to maintaining their hair.  This product is basically the cost of one visit to the hairdressers, and it is reusable.  It's a bargain!

title: My hair was adjusting pretty well to the new routine -- it rarely looked ...
text:
Do you ever have that feeling... when you realize, as you're first seeing, or tasting, or experiencing something, that you can't wait to tell everyone you know about what it?

THIS CREME IS THAT FOR ME!

About two months ago, I cut traditional shampoo out of my routine completely. Over the years of heavily shampooing my hair, it had gotten thin,
completely lacked shape or body, got excessively sweaty and oily with minimal physical activity, and I had to wash it once or twice a day to look decent. Absurd. Cutting back on sulfate-laden shampoo was my solution, but I had no patience for a gradual transition, so I quit cold turkey!

I used baking soda and water once or twice a week, depending on my schedule. My hair was adjusting pretty well to the new routine -- it rarely looked oily, and especially with some extensive brushing in the evenings to help redistribute oils, etc., I had body that I never used to have, and my hair felt and looked thicker and healthier. I also stopped getting super sweaty/oily/gross hair after working out, sleeping -- even walking my dog used to pretty much sabotage my hair.

However, it started to become evident that ALL the excessive oil/dirt was never really being washed out by my baking soda wash, and it was starting to get a little heavy. Each time I used the soda wash, it was cleaner than it had been, but probably not really clean enough. The ends were drying out from the soda wash, but the roots were heavy and thick. Suddenly my hair was starting to lose body again, because it was heavy and dense.

So I looked into how I wanted to proceed and decided that cowashing (washing with conditioner instead of shampoo) was a great alternative. I needed something to really be able to mix into my hair (water mixtures aren't great for that!) and soak each strand. I also needed to address the drying ends, and give my hair back the life it had been developing before getting (literally) weighed down. Also, to be honest, I also just missed the thoroughly clean feeling you get from drenching your hair in cleansing product and rinsing it out!

So I found Repure's Coconut Creme Cleansing Pudding -- in a pump bottle, nonetheless! I'm not normally a fan of coconut scented body products; they're usually pretty artificial and I find the smell a little overwhelming, but not the case here. The scent is light and refreshing; cleansing and relaxing. Natural.

I used about 10 or 11 pumps to TOTALLY soak my shoulder length, straight hair - the bottle recommends 8-10, which sounds like a lot, but they're pretty small pumps. Those 10/11 pumps that I opted to used are probably a lot for my length and texture -- I wanted to be able to completely saturate every inch, with a little extra left over. I wouldn't expect to have to use that many pumps every time.

As I'm rubbing it in, I'm excited. Smells great, feels great, seems promising. I let it sit as I went about my other business in the shower. Started rinsing it out. I can FEEL how silky smooth my hair is. I'm excited. This is it.

My hair dries quicker than it has been since starting no-poo -- it's clean! It's totally clean!

It finishes drying -- I have body. I have no excess oil. I have no dry ends. My hair is smoother than it's been in MONTHS, looks great, smells great. From an inexpensive, truly hair-friendly product.

Paraben free, sulfate, chloride and dye free, this "cleansing pudding" is a great option for shampoos and/or conditioners. I would have no desire to use a designated shampoo using this product, irrelevant of my relatively new-found dedication to no-poo.

I purchased this product based on a couple of reviews. When it came, I was in the midst of an outbreak on fingers of both hands. By the next day, I wasn't itchy, and the skin wasn't as inflamed. On the second night, the cracks had healed, and the scales were nearly gone. I've also used this on my heels, right before bedtime. My feet are now very smooth. And, I find the scent to be relaxing. It's almost like an herbal tea, and isn't overpowering at all.
I have been using this now for nearly a month, and haven't had another eczema outbreak. It's more than likely NOT a cure, but it's doing wonders at keeping the symptoms in check! I'm buying another container to keep at work, and another for my sister, who also suffers from eczema.

text:
DRY SKIN? READ THIS! I am very, very pleased to be able to write this review. Right now it is the month of March. The weather up here in Idaho is still chilly, but not freezing. I am originally from the Southeastern part of the U.S. and moved here almost two years ago. The first year my face was a bit dry from the Winters here, but not too bad. A little OTC moisturizer helped quite well. However, this second Winter season here, Whoa! Talk about dry skin! My husband (who is an ER physician) originally thought I developed ECZEMA on my body (turned out it wasn't eczema, its just severe dry skin). Around November I developed red, dry patches of skin on 50% of my face, both arms, inside my ear canals, and parts of my chest. I tried EVERYTHING over the counter (OTC), and NOTHING helped. title: Good for your head, so it's probably good if you have a furry face, too.
text:
Well, I can say I'm pretty impressed with this cordless trimmer, though I don't currently have a beard. I use it on my head to save the cost of haircuts, and from my first experience with it I can say it does a pretty good job. There's plenty of power to handle a whole head of hair, and the multi-height adjusting is a breeze with their built-in dial. I dialed it a little too low my first time, so I got a really close haircut, but now that I understand that they went with actual measurements instead of general guard numbers (I usually do a "3", but that does NOT correspond to the number 3 on this unit's dial) I can adjust accordingly. I even managed to cut the back of my head without much fuss. Of course, the reason this uses actual measurements instead of comb sizes is because it's meant for beard AND head, and when you're trimming a beard you're much more concerned with each and every half-milometer of hair.

The only negative I could see was that I had to remove the plastic guard and clear out hair every few strokes, otherwise it wouldn't cut due to being completely jammed up with hair. The guard kind of accumulates it, but luckily it's removed easily and cleared out with a few taps.

I'm very happy with the recharger, which doesn't have a cord. It's just a plug-in base that goes right into your wall socket. My bathroom counter is already covered in other things, and I am happy not to have to hook up another corded device. With this, you charge it right up on the wall socket, and it takes up no counter space. When you're done you remove it and store it easily, since it's so small.

All in all, this is an excellent trimmer for giving yourself a nice short haircut. I can only imagine it works great on a beard, too.

text:
UPDATE 7/28: I now have both the blue cap and pink cap. I use the pink one to remove regular stuff, and the blue for the tougher stuff. My same long wear lipstick didn't come off with the with pink, but with the blue again only took 3 swipes! Seriously I am floored!! Just make sure you shake vigorously to mix it evenly.

Wow. I think I may have found my holy grail makeup remover! I used it for the first time on a "full glam" face as I went to a pretty important event. I'm talking long wear cream eye shadow, long wear 24 hour liquid lipstick, and a double dose of setting pray. The whole nine-yards. And this stuff took care of it all. This bottle (blue cap) is bi-phase, so it has the oil looking stuff (no it's not oil) floating at the top of the bottle. It did not feel greasy, or heavy at all. For my eye makeup I held a soaked cotton round over my eye for a few seconds and I would say 85% of it came off with the first few swipes. Even my mascara. No eyelash loss either. It also did not sting my eyes. Then I did the residual clean up with another soaked piece of cotton. The thing that literally made me say "WOW" out loud, was my lipstick removal. I have been wearing the same stuff for years and it stays all day/night with zero transfer, but it can be a pain to get every last trace of it removed. In just three swipes, my lipstick was gone! And no heavy rubbing or scrubbing! I am TOTALLY sold on this stuff! I ended up using it all over my face to remove everything else, and it felt lightweight and clean, but "a bit much" for my face. I did use my Simple Brand Micellar to fully clean everything off as I prefer my anti-aging face cream. But I'm sure this would be great for those with dry skin to just leave as is and go to bed. WONDERFUL PRODUCT! Make sure you shake well each time you pour it.

title: Tom Ford's Grey Vetiver is a masterpiece..!!
text:
For those looking for an entry level niche fragrance, look no more - TF Grey Vetiver is a great starting point. That was me about a year ago when I took that "leap of faith", not to mention, paying the extra $$$ (USD), for Tom Ford's Noir. I haven't looked back..!!

TFGV is a clean, fresh, and "outdoorsy" fragrance that portrays class, eloquence, and masculinity. Grey Vetiver provides above average longevity, lasting about 6 to 8 hours on my skin, and even longer on clothing. The projection/sillage is modest, however, this might not be a bad thing - my girlfriend loves the fragrance and frequently suggests that she only smells it when she enters "my space" - I am totally good with her being in "my space"..!! Additionally, this might work out well in an office environment where the is no danger of the fragrance being offensive. GV provides great flexibility - I am comfortable wearing daily in the office (yes, I do wear a suit and tie..), to more formal events, or even the casual outings. While most reviewers suggest Spring and Summer for wear, given the "outdoorsy" notes of vetiver, I respectfully disagree - I like it in Fall and Winter (too..).

The bottle and packaging are first class. I am especially fond of the bottle - something about it that exudes confidence. Well done, Mr. Ford. While probably still at the lower end of niche fragrances, the price/value is below average, but I would suggest that you cannot place a value on compliments and confidence while wearing the fragrance. You will not be disappointed...

My final tally for Tom Ford's Grey Vetiver is 4.5 stars out of 5. This is a first class scent that everyone should have in their collection.

Enjoy your day and make it count... Invest your time rather than wasting it..

title: Used it on our family of 5 for a year, switched to a cheaper product, but we're switching back
text:
***UPDATE: I wrote this review before using the reformulated Earthpaste which now includes Xylitol. We were having the great results described below with Earthpaste, so we purchased more after a break, only to discover the toothpaste we received was more watery and contained xylitol compared to the previous formulation. Not sure whether this will affect our opinion of the product as we haven't used it long yet.***

We decided to use flouride-free toothpaste for our family of 5 for a year to see what difference it would make. Our dental health was probably average before we began. Here's the breakdown: husband brushes 2x daily but doesn't go to dental cleanings regularly, wife and kids ages 3-8 brush at bedtime and goes to dental cleanings regularly. No one flosses unless needed. Husband and wife had mild sensitivities to cold in teeth at the start of this 'experiment', kids had varying amounts of (or lack of) cavities. The older 2 kids had been on fluoride toothpaste, but the youngest hadn't yet. We did not take steps to remove fluoride from the city tap water we use for drinking and cooking.

Initial response: "Ewwww, this toothpaste is brown," chime the kids. We quickly discover that only the lemon flavored earthpaste is mild enough for the younger two kids to use. After protesting the appearance, we all had to get used to the lack of foam. I expected this in advance and was glad we weren't putting foaming agents (unnecessary chemicals) into our mouths, but it still took a week or so to get used to. I like all the flavors in this order: cinnamon, lemon, wintergreen, peppermint. I am familiar with essential oils, do not promote ingesting them, and tell my kids to spit out this toothpaste when they are done brushing so I don't freak out about the wintergreen essential oil. You should be training your kids to spit out the toothpaste anyway because it is dislodging food particles and built up bacteria that they shouldn't be digesting, even though the toothpaste is deemed 'edible' by the manufacturer. This also teaches your kids to be in the habit to spit toothpaste so if they ever end up using fluoride (they forget their toothpaste when they go to Grandma's and she gives them a tube of hers, etc), they will automatically spit it out.

Long term results: Within a month, we realized our teeth felt "good." Not necessarily "better," but we were a bit concerned they'd go downhill without the flouride coating they were so used to. Then my husband had a nasty cavity come through, must've been brewing for a long time. Part of his tooth broke off and he continued oil pulling with coconut oil (swishing coconut oil in your mouth 20 minutes daily and then spitting it into the garbage) to cope until it could be repaired. We heard about X-Factor Gold High-Vitamin Butter Oil by Green Pasture from a friend who said taking it in conjunction with oil pulling helped heal and fill in cavities naturally. Broken tooth didn't bother him and actually filled in over 50% of the hole with new bone. I tried getting pictures of this to blog because we just could not believe it was actually working- we are skeptics of natural health claims as much as we are of flouride. However, it wasn't a front tooth and so between lighting and trying to hold my husband's cheek back while taking photos it didn't work out too well. Research. Evidence. Here was our evidence that our body can repair itself when not being hindered, but rather supplied. He fell off the wagon oil-pulling and his tooth would hurt a bit but the regrown bone stayed in place (we could see it was regrown because it was lighter in color than the existing tooth). Appointment to fix tooth came around and it was repaired without issue. Dentist discouraged our use of non-flouride toothpaste as well as our declining fluouride treatments for our family at the dental office, but at this point we were convinced to give it a whole year's go of it.

After about 2 months of using Earthpaste, we'd fallen off the wagon of oil pulling because it was just cumbersome to remember and fit in our routine. We both noticed that our teeth were not as sensitive to cold as they had been. All temperature sensitivity was gone within 3 months of using this toothpaste. (From my understanding and research, you won't have the same remineralization effects if you are using fluoride mouthwash, you need to keep your mouth a flouride-free zone as much as possible.)

At the end of our year's experiment, we had no intentions of turning back, the area in my mouth the dentist had been watching for a cavity to form never developed into anything. One kid had a clean check up with no cavities and another kid with very tight teeth had a check up with 4 cavities. We decided to switch to a different fluoride-free toothpaste since it would be cheaper and we noted that Earthpaste changed its formula to include xylitol, which we had desired to avoid. Since we'd be getting xylitol in Earthpaste, why not switch to a cheaper xylitol toothpaste? We did, and after 1 month of using Xyli-white (we were actually grossed out by the foaming and had to re-adjust to the sensation, but we got over that), we discovered that both of us were experiencing mild sensitivity to cold and a general feeling that our teeth just weren't as good feeling. Little aches or a feeling of them just not being 'clean enough.'

So, we're back to ordering Earthpaste. (Also, we're still using soft-bristle toothbrushes, still not flossing regularly, and still brushing the same number of times per day as we did when this started. Just had to add that info for the other researchers/skeptics out there. Another note- don't expect great results if you drink large amounts of sugar (in coffee, soda, etc) daily, either! But you can research all that yourself.)

title: great for a decent clean but not really deep clean
text:
I have to admit, I'm not always the best at cleaning my make-up brushes - I tend to brush them off a lot on tissues or even my hand to clean off the lingering eyeshadow or blush, and once a month or so give them a good clean with a brush cleaner. So I figured I'd give Ecotools' cloths a try. These remind me of wipes you'd use to clean your face of make-up, they have a similar texture and come in a resealable pouch, aren't too moist (they're not soaked through with the cleaner) and you don't want to be too rough with them. I used them on my eyeshadow brushes and my lip brush, and they do a decent job of cleaning off the make-up, especially from the lip brush. And like those wipes, they're good for when you're not in the mood to do a really thorough cleaning.

I think they say 'daily' use because yes, they'll be great for cleaning up after any daily product, in helping you 'reset' your brushes, especially if you like using a lot of different color palettes (I know I have a lot of different eyeshadow palettes and switch between neutrals and bright shades all the time). What these won't do is give a really deep clean - you'll have to stick to the cleaning bars or cleansers to do that every week or month or whatever. But if you want to take something with you on the go or use when you're switching things up, yes, these will work really well, and you can use one cloth for several brushes. Just don't think these will give a truly deep clean. And I'd put these in a ziplock bag or something to ensure that they don't dry out between use as even though they're 'resealable', it's not the greatest seal to keep them airtight.

title: Magic!
text:
I have been looking for the best beard products in three categories for a very long time. I've spent a small fortune trying to find the best all natural wash, wax and conditioner (balm/butter). I never thought that I could find them all under the same label.

I've written a review of their wax here on Amazon but just to touch on that, it's the best! It's a very firm hold wax while still being usable in the beard. The best part is that it lasts all day. I haven't yet tried their wash but that's next and if they've nailed it like the rest that will be amazing. It's currently only available on their site, I hope it hits prime soon.

On to the balm, this stuff is magic! If you told me that it was canned Pegasus butter, I'd believe you. As I said above, I use their wax during the day for styling but it's not a conditioning product nor is that it's intent. With that, I've been looking for the best overnight conditioner that uses all natural quality ingredients. Well, here it is. This stuff conditions your beard like nothing you've ever used. I'm well beyond the itch so I can't comment on that, though I'm sure it helps as it's very soothing.

The ingredients are top notch, all natural and exactly what you want to see. I have to admit, their label does make this look like another mass produced chemical product (sorry) but I can assure you, this is hand crafted, small batch quality stuff.

The consistency of this balm is not really that of a balm but more of a butter/batter. I actually prefer this for conditioning products. Oil is too; oily and causes breakouts. Balms are too dry/thick and don't get down in there very well. I've never been impressed with oils or balms when it comes to conditioning. A butter really gets in there and clings to the hair and skin.

A quick word on moisturizers. They don't actually moisturize. What they do is keep moisture from escaping. The best at their job are the thick ones that stick around such as petroleum jelly, believe it or not. But no one wants that on their skin all day.

This stuff sticks around and is great on the skin as well as the beard. However, it stays a bit greasy so I wouldn't wear it on the bare skin during the day. Some may find it a bit too greasy even on the beard though it's not bad. It's far less greasy in the beard after a few hours. I haven't had any irritation or breakouts either.

This is not a styling product and I wish there was a standard for beard product naming. Balms typically offer a modicum of styling ability, though this again is really a butter and not intended for styling. That said, some may find it has a light capacity for that depending on their beard. If this is an all in one product for you, consider yourself very lucky!

The scent I actually like. Their website describes it as “birthday cake” and I can see that, if you hold that in your mind while smelling it. I would say that this smells like “cool mint play-dough”. Some may find that they don't like the play-dough undertone but I don't mind at all. Actually, as good as this works, no one should. Especially since the smell dissipates in less than an hour.

This is great stuff and for my use as an overnight conditioner, it's perfect. I have also found that if you use their wax first, comb it in, then use this balm, it's creates a kind of medium hold conditioning balm. This may be perfect for some. You can also use the balm first for easier wax application and a lighter hold or rub them together for a similar effect.

Overall great conditioning product that is best used overnight.

title: Your face is worth it!!!
text:
This sunscreen has changed me forever: For the first time in my life, I am actually using sun protection on a daily basis.
I'm a super pale redhead with very sensitive skin and I've never been able to stand anything on my face – not sunscreen, not makeup, not moisturizer, not sunglasses, nothing. I've probably tried over a hundred different sunscreens over my 50+ years of life and I just can't tolerate the feeling of something sitting on top of my skin, like having my face smothered by cling wrap.
This stuff is different. It's very light – it's not like a lotion or cream that holds its shape when you squeeze it out of the tube; you have to be careful, because it's basically a liquid and will run down your fingers. It goes on smooth, absorbs easily, and doesn't burn or sting my skin or eyes. It's fragrance free and after I rub it in, it feels like ... nothing. If I touch my face it feels smooth, but I can't feel the product itself covering the surface of my skin. At all. It's a miracle!
Yes, it's expensive. And when you see the bottle, it'll probably be smaller than you were imagining. However: you only have one face! Just try one bottle – you can afford that, right? If you don't love it, you can always go back to whatever you were using before.
But if you're like me, and you were using NOTHING before, because you just can't stand anything touching your skin, this stuff could be a game changer. It has been for me.
Full disclosure: I have touched my own face about seven or eight times while writing this review, because I'm still so astonished that I'm actually wearing sunscreen, on my face, and it actually feels good!

Editing my review April 2016 for fellow sufferers: I have found after doing TONS of research trying to find the answers to hair loss that it is important to have a sufficient Ferritin levels (ask your doctor to check your blood), I started taking Iron purchased here on Amazon-Solargar Gentle Iron, 25 mg). After that, they were ready for polish! (I applied gel and chrome). These nails stayed put for a few days and I applied a little bit of glue on the corners (not because they were loosening up, but because I'm just paranoid like that). I learned later that this was NOT necessary.

About a week later, I wanted to change them because the gel polish I applied over it started to chip (cheap gel polish, ugh!) and wow... these were so hard to remove! I only soaked them for about 5 minutes but I was supposed to soak them for longer because when I tried to remove it, it was very difficult. This also proves how strong these nails would have stayed adhered if I kept them on longer. These nails are easy to use and apply. Next time, I'll just file it down a bit so it's not as long and apply better gel polish!

title: Pretty good – NOT an antiperspirant though!
text:
These came up on a lightning deal a little while ago for about half their normal cost and I thought, why not? Summer’s coming, I’m doing some travel, might be a nice addition to my purse. And, they kind of are. They feel refreshing and cooling on a hot day. The scent is unobtrusive, kind of a subtle fresh/citrusy smell, and I don’t think it would bother anyone with allergies like some scents do.

One thing to keep in mind that’s not really mentioned anywhere on the product description page on Amazon – these do NOT contain antiperspirant! They will not make you sweat less! In case you’re not aware – the “deodorant” you use in the morning to keep you dry and non-smelly through the day typically contains two main things – deodorant (for the smell), and anti-perspirant (which is pretty self-explanatory). So, these are not really a full-time replacement for your normal deodorant.

I’ve knocked a star off for a couple of reasons: the lack of notice in the product description about not containing an antiperspirant (which could lead people to believe it’s a natural replacement for their everyday “deodorant”), and secondly, they seem to be getting less and less effective. The smell doesn’t last as long as it did when I first started using them. It’s possible it’s because it’s so much hotter now and I’m actually sweating the scent off, or maybe I’ve just gotten so used to the smell I’ve gone nose-blind to it. Who knows…I will continue to use them, and if they come up cheap again I’ll get some more, but I don’t think I’ll pay full price for them, especially when I could use a scented baby wipe to kind of do the same thing.

Also – absolutely no change in my underarm hair growth (I was incredibly skeptical about that claim, so I’m not surprised about that :))

These are horrible, do not waste your money. I was THRILLED to find these recently at a drugstore, as they are a fantastic idea. I know it sounds ridiculous but that's basically what this product is - ridiculous and won't work in any way. The only way I can see these working is if another person is painting your nails for you, and THEY apply these to your nails. But if that was happening there would be no need for this product in the first place.

Ugh, such a waste of time and money, so annoying. Please save your money, time, and sanity, don't buy these.

title: Bobbi Brown is good, but there are many others, too if you follow some basic guidelines
text:
I bought Bobbi Brown Luminous Foundation as I usually do, in the color I use. Now I see my order has been been cancelled.The sellers I bought from are *out* of the color I use. I do think it is a good product. But please, DO NOT be fooled into thinking it is a great product and that the one ounce they are selling is worth more than $45-$50. There are a lot of excellent foundations out there. Over the past year or more, Bobbi Brown changed this foundation. It is NOT the one I began using five years ago. Now, it seems Bobbi Brown is coming out with more foundations and discontinuing this, and these greedy sellers are gouging people. DON'T let that happen. Estee Lauder makes an excellent foundation that has a dewy finish, not at all oily, called Lucidity. Check out the ratings on that at Nordstrom or other department stores. Christian Dior makes a fine foundation with better sunscreen and if you read up and stay up on your skin news, you know that nothing more than sunscreen will keep you looking great. It is pathetic that this is happening as I see some of these prices. Remember the names of those doing this. Know too that Bobbi Brown altered this foundation a little more than a year ago making it more yellow, so this is likely why the company is discontinuing it.
A good foundation should have 1) SPF that is AT LEAST 15 and you should still put sunscreen of at least 30 SPF on beneath it. A good oil-free is made my Peter Thomas Roth and DDF (sunscreens) and a good foundation should have enough colors to work well with your coloring. 3) It should also be available in oil free and with excellent moisturizers, not cheap mineral oil. That said, know there are many excellent choices out there, ranging in various prices. There also are some excellent tinted moisturizers with SPF. A little powder over that with some dewy blush and you are good to go. If you need more coverage and are oil prone, there is mineral powder. There are so many options, you NEVER should be gouged. If you are new to using foundation, it's no a bad idea to go to a high-end store like Nordstrom and sit with a cosmetics department person and have her or him show you various foundations, recommend colors best for you (we can't always tell ourselves) and you can tell them what feels comfortable, what you like (no heavy feeling etc.) and get that professional touch then you can buy yourself and grow more confident to try different foundations on your own.
The best advice I got when I was younger was you should not skimp on foundation. Buy a good one, usually found in department stores like Bobbi Brown, Clinique, Smashbox, Estee Lauder, Christian Dior, Urban Decay, MAC, I mean the list goes on and on and on. You can get things like mascara at the drug store, because they never last long anyway. But foundation, lipstick, and eye shadow -- go high end. You can find a lot of those other brands here, too, sold by people who will be reasonable in their pricing. This is a shame the prices are getting ridiculous DON'T fall for it. You CAN find another foundation you will love just as much.

title: This works if used correctly
text:
I understand why there are so many low star reviews but I also wonder if they used this product correctly. My first five attempts were total garbage, it got better from there with more experimentation. The keys for me were:
I used a peel off base coat so I could practice repeatedly without suffocating on polish remover.
Used a polish color underneath that I wouldn't mind peaking through the foil.
Applied an even and thin layer of adhesive.
Let dry thoroughly, though it will still be tacky and soft to touch, part of why aggressive layer needed to be thin.
Apply foil shiny side up.
Press hard. No, I mean really, really hard. Silicone tools help but I also did ok just using pressure from fingers.
Pay attention to getting tips and around the cuticle. I pressed extra hard around cuticle area to crease foil which made it easier to remove without ripping up foil from adhesive.
Pull the foil up quickly and smoothly. If you've waxed it is similar to that motion.
It worked well when I was careful to do it exactly like that being careful and thorough at each step.

Good luck finding a top coat that doesn't eat the foil. I've tried about a half dozen with varying degrees of success/ failure. The foil lasting only a few hours and disappearing in water and being eaten by to coat is not a failure of the adhesive.

title: GREAT MOISTURIZER TO USE INSTEAD OF LA MER
text: I give Crème de La Mer one STAR because of its astronomical price.  I'm 53 years old and was a La Mer devotee for more than a decade until it became so unbelievably cost prohibitive.  Unless there's a diamond at the bottom of the jar after the cream is used up, the skyrocketing price simply can't be justified for the less than stellar results.  This cream can TEMPORARILY diminish the appearance of wrinkles, but so can a severely less expensive effective moisturizer, which I'll get to in a minute.  I've also tried the German-manufactured Nivea cream that others have touted as a La Mer replacement but found it to be too greasy and, frankly, it didn't do quite the same job as La Mer.  So, I did some research at my local drug store and decided to try Loreal Collagen...I liked the collagen part.  And, thus, my La Mer spell was broken!!  I've been using Loreal Collagen now for the past few years and, frankly, I don't miss La Mer AT ALL -- especially the out of this world price.  Drug stores sell Loreal Collagen jars for about $15 each; you can find it on Amazon for even less.  Compare that to hundreds of dollars for a small jar of La Mer, and there's simply no earthly justification to purchase La Mer.

title: Deceptive Marketing
text: This is deceptive marketing. Good ingredients, but you cannot call this Argan Oil; that is not honest. The overwhelming amount of oil here is safflower oil, the same as you would purchase in Whole Foods. Safflower oil costs the company 15 cents an oz. That is why the price seems relatively inexpensive, but in fact it is expensive. If someone labels their product Argan Oil, and there are hundreds of companies who do to take advantage of its reputation, they should put the percentages of oils on the label so consumers can make an intelligent decision. There is a huge health and beauty industry that caters to women's needs and desires, but which is deceptive in its marketing and labeling.

title: Long & strong!
text:
First off...I have been dealing with not so great nails over the past year or so. They break easy, peel, and some of my nails have pits in them. I started taking biotin supplements, which made them grow...but did not make them stronger. They still broke! Then I tried Sally Hansen Hard As Nails for a few months. My nails responded a little better, but still chipped and broke easy.

Eventually I found OPI Original Nail Envy. Amazing! My nails grew like crazy--they were stronger and even sharper. But after a few applications my nail beds began to ache, and I noticed white spots underneath my nails which indicated that my nails were separating from my nail beds! Ahh! I did some research on Nail Envy had this affect on some people. I was stuck with crappy nails again.

I've tried everything else--forgoing nail polish completely, switching from acetone remover to non-acetone, focusing on cuticle care, but nothing worked. I stumbled upon Nailtiques one night somewhere on the internet and thought I'd give it a try. Here's my review! (finally!)

I purchased Nailtiques Formula 2 off Amazon. I cut my nails short to monitor the growth, just to see if it would work. After applying Nailtiques every day for a week, my nails had the average amount of growth that I normally experience, but without the breaking or peeling. I removed all of the Nailtiques and gave my nails a break for one night. Then I began the routine again the next day.

This was 4 weeks ago. Ever since the end of week 2 my nails have been long and strong! I've had to cut them twice now to keep them at a manageable length...since I have never had long nails before! I apply Nailtiques Formula 2 every day, and I have also purchased their cuticle cream and the Forumla 2 Plus for my "problem" nails (my two pointer fingernails which chipped during my Nailtiques-free day). This stuff is really amazing. It's so weird to look down at my now lady-like hands and my beautiful long nails. They even passed the ultimate test---peeling off the plastic that seals condiment bottles! lol
