title: Professional results, everything you need in one set
text:
Having problem blackheads, I have bought just about every tool on the market trying to remove them. This set is by far the most effective set I have ever used.
The set comes with four pieces and a carrying case. The set contains one large spoon, one small spoon, two needles, a triangle loop, angled loop and a wide loop. So, you even though it's four tools, they each have a tool at each end which really makes it an eight piece set.
This is not only great for black heads but, blemishes of any type! White heads, ingrown hairs and even ear wax blockage. Be sure to clean/sterilize the tools and areas you intend to treat. I like to use a good facial cleanser first. I will then steam my face or whatever area I need to remove the blemish from. I have a facial steamer but, you can boil a pot of water and stand over it (carefully of course) for a few minutes. You can even take a very hot shower and that's good enough steam to really bring the blackheads, etc... to the surface. These tools are so effective you really do not need to apply very much pressure at all to remove the black/white heads. I love the needle ends, when you have a very stubborn hard to "pop" blackhead, you can give a small "prick" and then use one of the loops to press it out. It normally takes me 1-2 hours to clear my entire face, with these tools I was able to clear every visible blemish in 25 minutes! After you have removed all of your blackheads, wash again and towel dry.
I have a 14 year old daughter, she gets horrible blackheads in her ears from wearing earbuds. These tools have been such a helpful tool in safely, effective and most importantly pain-free removal of these stubborn blackheads. If you have problematic skin or a teenager in your home, this is a must have kit!
The tools are very well made and extremely durable. I love the in the center, the metal has some engraved gripping area to ensure your hands stay perfectly in place with no slipping! Very easy to care for, i wash with hot water and a little fish soap and wipe down with alcohol. I make sure to dry the tools completely before storing.

title: Painless!
text:
Spring is here. Decided to try out the wax I got from CVS a while back. I took their suggestion and patted some baby powder on since I do live in humid temperature. My underarms have always given me headaches. I used to have to ice them to reduce the pain and minimize irritation after waxing. (And sometime even after that they would still scar). I used a thick layer (esp. on the edges) as seen in the pictures and waited a minute or two after I applied it. Then I tested it with my fingers and found that they didn't stick anymore, so I just ripped it off (making sure I had a good grip on the whole bottom edge). To my surprise (since I did read these reviews about it being painful), it didn't hurt at all. The picture of my arm was taken RIGHT after the removal. I didn't clean it yet, and as evident on the picture, there was very little amount of residue because the edges were thick enough to not tear. The cleaning of the residue was very easy. I just lathered on some baby oil and it came right off. (Even from my fingers and nails).

Yes, it did take longer to microwave, but the instructions did indicate that you may need more time (increments of 30 seconds). But this was a VERY small price to pay for painless removal.

Don't let the reviews scare you!! It's incredible.

Note: I forgot the powder on the other arm, so it stuck on just a tad more than with powder, but a quick layer of aloe took the twinge of pain away.

TL;DR review: this is great stuff and my tattoo healed very quickly but go easy on it 😎

pros: petroleum-free, packed with great ingredients(calendula, thyme, comfrey, vitamin e), and I love how it smells. It has this interesting thyme/pine/almost antiseptic smell that reminds me a little of whatever my artist used to clean my fresh tattoo.

cons: The only reason I gave this 4 stars instead of 5 is that it’s a little heavy... it’s easy to use too much. One edge of my tattoo(heavy blackwork on my forearm) was more sensitive and red than the rest and I slowed the healing by not realizing how much I was putting on it.

***I take full responsibility for using too much product*** All i’m saying is that because it’s sheer and natural and I was so wowed by it that I didn’t realized I was using too much.

All this being said, after two and half weeks my tattoo is bold and bright- it’s healed beautifully and very quickly, especially once I eased up. buy this stuff! 🖤

title: This is a lovely night cream best suited for normal/combination or stressed skin
text:
This is a lovely night cream best suited for normal/combination or stressed skin. I mainly purchased it because it contains Manuka Honey. I love using honey in skincare because of its moisturizing and ant-inflammatory properties and manuka honey is said to have special anti-bacterial activity. In addition the cream contains sweet almond oil for emolliency, rosemary extract which has anti-aging and anti-inflammatory benefits, vitamin A (repairing skin damage) and the "botox" peptide, acetyl hexapeptide-8.

The cream comes in a standard jar with a twist-off cap. It seems like it would be heavy going on but absorbs pretty quickly and actually gives my somewhat dry skin a matte finish. It is moisturizing but I think the real benefits of this cream are for calming and anti-stress. I ordinarily use a very emollient night cream, almost like a sleeping mask, to provide moisture to my dry skin. I also periodically use high percentage glycolic acid products to give my skin an occasional peel. After I do this, I need to treat my skin very carefully or else I break out or get rashes. This cream is perfect for calming and de-stressing my skin and the anti-inflammatory/anti-bacterial properties ensure my skin recovers quickly. Scent is very natural, I can smell honey and a slight herbal undertone but dissipates quickly on application. I'm happy to add this to my arsenal of skincare products!

Ingredients: Aqua,Prunus Amygdalus Dulcis (Sweet Almond) Oil, Glycerin,Glyceryl Searate,,Acetyl Hexapeptide-8, Manuka Honey,Stearic Acid,Cetyl Alcohol,Phenoxyethanol,Lanolin, Ginkgo Biloba, Leaf Extract,Panax Ginseng Root, Extract,Titanium,Dioxide,Tocopheryl,Acetate,Sodium Hydroxide, Sodium Hyaluronate,Ethylhexylglycerin,Parfum,Retinyl Palmitate,Rosmarinus Officinalis (Rosemary ) Leaf Extract.

title: Nice light scent for daily wear
text:
I love to discover new scents, hence why I hound Ross's and TJ Maxx for their discounted perfumes. I had never tried Lacoste before, so I took the plunge, even though it said it had "coconut" and if there is one scent I've grown to hate, it's coconut.

But seriously, this perfume is a fantastic "day to day" perfume! It's light and subtle, a perfect balance between sweet and floral. I don't smell coconut at all, which is absolutely perfect!

This is definitely not a super strong perfume, but really, that's good because those strong perfumes tend to get rather noxious (and make me nauseous) over time.

I really like the packaging - very efficient with little waste. Same with the bottle - while I do love my decorative bottles, I appreciate streamlined ones that fit into cabinets better.

Overall, I do like the scent; I find it very light and refreshing, more floral though than coconut. If that sounds like something you want, head to your perfume counter and check it out!

*C.S. Light*

title: caution: product has been re-formulated
text:
i submit this review as a warning to others who, like myself, have allergic reactions to most deodorants. i was a loyal user of nature's gate "autumn breeze" for years without a problem; in fact it was one of the very few brands that i did not experience adverse effects from (and that actually worked). i was quite disappointed when it was discontinued and relieved when it was available again, but, unbeknownst to me, they had re-formulated it and i ended up with by far the worst burning rash i've ever had from a deodorant of any kind, "natural" or otherwise, that lasted for several days after i stopped using it. i had to use about every remedy known to man to function through this reaction; i couldn't believe it was from this brand which i had used for so long, so i gave it another shot. same effect, worse even. but of course, there was no indication on the package (unless you count comparing the ingredients with one of the old ones) or in any of the sales/product information that the product had been changed since its previous version. they should have at least provided that.
also their customer service was not helpful in this matter -- said they would "have this matter investigated" but did not offer any refund for the six sticks that i had bought immediately after the hiatus of this product. take responsibility for your product, nature's gate! i guess my advice would be not to do what i did and stock up right away -- try one first and see how it goes.

title: Good Cream, Good Ingredients
text:
Taylor of Old Bond Street's Sandalwood shaving cream lathers and performs pretty well. However, the cream is a little hard to squeeze out of the tube. As you squeeze it, it almost feels as though it has dried up inside. Once it comes out, you'll notice that the cream is just fine after you start to mix it. I'm not quite sure why this is. On a brighter note, I do find it to be less runny than Eton, St. James, and Mr. Taylors in a tube. I prefer the tubes overall as I find them to be a little more convenient for travel, usage and storage.

Sandalwood seems to be a popular scent among the wet shaving community so I wanted to see what all the hype was about. Well, I learned that I'm not a huge fan of sandalwood but I still enjoy using this cream. The performance is very good and the scent is not unpleasant by any means; it just seems a bit cloying. If you haven't smelled it before, it's heavy on the sweet, old-fashioned soapy smell. It might be the perfect scent for someone who enjoys sweet, woody, oud-type fragrances. If that sounds like you, then give this a shot.

One thing that I love about Taylors is that they don't use parabens in their products. It makes me feel better about what I'm slathering on my face over the years which is one less thing to worry about. So the tube and the ingredients are convenient for me. The scent is pleasing enough, although I'll stay away from Sandalwood aftershaves and colognes. And although it's not the thickest cream I've used, it does lather and protect without any issues. For now, I'll give this the four stars that I feel it deserves. It really is a decent shaving cream. With all the shaving products out there, you could do a lot worse.

title: Un...be...lievable
text:
I was trying to research a new luxury shampoo when I ran across an article suggesting this scalp treatment. I was apprehensive to buy it because it wasn't what I was looking for. But the more I thought about it, the more I realized that my scalp has been dry and it has itched. And it's actually been pretty bad for a very long time.

I ordered this stuff and really wasn't sure how to use it when it arrived. Right away, I was definitely impressed with the aroma. It smells amazing. I was kind of shaking it over my head and letting it drip. But I finally decided to start pressing the tip right into my scalp all over. I didn't really know when to stop but eventually I figured I'd used enough and starting massaging it in with my fingers.

Another review mentions a tingle and the ad above mentions a heating sensation may occur. For me, the sensation was exponentially different. I felt like I'd fallen victim to one of Kevin's boobie traps in Home Alone. It was as if a blow torch had completely lit the top of my head on fire. I went back into the bathroom to make sure my hair was still there. I thought that maybe it had completely burned off. But with raised shoulders and eyebrows and clinched teeth, I waited out the burn. I shampooed my hair and was surprised that later that night my scalp seemed to be a little better already.

I waited 4 days before feeling brave enough to give this stuff another try. This time, the burn was nowhere near as intense. But when my hair dried I noticed a lot of light flakes. For hours it bothered me. I finally put some baby oil on my head and went to bed.

I woke up the next day, washed my hair, and am just absolutely blown away by how good my scalp feels. I just did another treatment and feel virtually no burn at all. This stuff is truly amazing. I figure that the products I've used in my hair have created pretty uncomfortable scalp issues for about 15 years and this miracle elixir cleared it up in 5 days. I have short hair. I don't know if I've even used 80% of the bottle. This is totally worth the price and I'd pay a lot more for it if I had to for my next bottle.

title: Hands down the best mascara I've ever tried
text:
I was pleasantly surprised by this mascara. I purchased it based on the recommendation of a friend and I'm glad I spent extra for BLINC. I have had no issues with the liquid splattering out like some users mentioned. When I asked my friend if she'd ever experienced this she said she had not either.

The way everybody describes "tubes" on your lashes did NOT match what I envisioned. I thought this hard little tubes would literally slide off your lashes that you could hold and examine. This is not at all the case. To remove the mascara, you only use warm water and gently rub your lashes. This causes the mascara tubes to get wet and soft turning it a bit like slimy feathers that just clump together and come right off in one good rub of the eyelashes. You just dump them down the drain (I hope it's OK for my drain!), but maybe they should be dumped into the trash bin? I don't know.

There is ZERO residue after removing the mascara. ZERO chance of having raccoon eyes later. It truly is amazing. I do have to say, however, that some tiny "shreds" can still end up on your upper cheeks after a long day, especially if you're an eye rubber, like me. It doesn't make raccoon eyes, but some flakes can still end up on your face, which took me by surprise as I didn't see any other reviewers mention that.

Pro Tip: apply one coat of mascara to entire set of lashes (you can even do lower lashes with this mascara!). Wait 30 seconds and take a dry cotton swab (Q-tip) and rub off any mascara that you accidentally got onto your skin (I usually manage to get mascara onto my lids whenever I apply it). No need to wet it or reapply eyeshadow after wiping off excess mascara with a Q-tip. It wipes right off without any smudging.

Second Pro Tip: don't use eye makeup remover. It's completely unnecessary and you'll still have to use the warm water technique afterwards anyway. It's so easy to remove, but amazingly stays on when you don't want it to come off!

While you only get one type of lashes - your own, but slightly thicker and longer - this is good enough for me. If you're expecting feathered lashes or whatever crazy style of eyelashes other mascara brands promise, you won't get that with BLINC. BLINC simply takes your own lashes and makes them appear longer, thicker, darker. No other crazy promises.

All mascara should be made this way. I cannot recommend this mascara highly enough.

Light Mountain has a more coarse grind than BAQ ( Body Art Quality ) henna, but there is a reason I prefer it. It is the most reasonably priced, SAFE henna on the market. Meaning, it's thoroughly tested for contaminants and is Organic. No chemical salts or metals etc in this box or any other they sell, and that is extremely important to me. title: Either way I have a superb watch...
text:
The watch is a tool watch. I have owned several Tudors, including the circa 70's reference 9121. This Tudor comes at an interesting time in Tudors lineage. They are now manufacturing their own in house movement with a silicon escapement, the MT 5621. Traditionally, they used the ETA movements in most of their watches. Or, in the case of my other Tudor, the Valijoux 7750, which is a chronograph. Tudor has 2 models available with the "new" movement, the North Flag, which is a new model altogether, featuring the MT 5621, and the PELAGOS, which is still on shelves selling with the "old" ETA 2824, as well as a version with the "new" in house MT5621. I imagine their eventual goal is to place as many of their own movements as possible into their watches. This is only speculation, as I am not privy to the strategic planning occurring as they continue to drive the TUDOR ship onward.
So, when I decided to purchase my Tudor, I chose the Ranger, still powered by the veritable workhorse ETA 2824. It will be interesting what history will say regarding this eventual shift into their own movements. The Ranger is perhaps the best value for a very high quality, all around field watch. Encased in a Rolex case, with screw down crown and once again powered by what is perhaps the most prominent ETA movement of the 20th century, the 2824 ETA. So, in essence, you can't go wrong with this choice. True to form, a straightforward no frills form follows function reliable, tough, enduring precise watch you can depend on in virtually any circumstance. Although not designed as a dive watch, it is quite capable of 150 meters or 500 feet, which simply put is at least 50 times the depth most humans will ever take it. IE, the deep end of a swimming pool. In fact, it is a better quality watch than many dive watches available.

So, the two watches that are available retail are the Pelagos, and the North Flag, both with the new MT 5621, and the Pelagos still widely available fitted with the ETA 2824. Once again, an interesting time in TUDORS history. Tudor makes no effort whatsoever to explain this to the general public. Nor do they try to hide, nor should they. I chose simply to put my money on a very tested combination. I have a North Flag on layaway, FYI. Because being both a collector and a gambler, I thought it best to hedge on the possibility that the MT5621 will be a true collectors piece, being the first Batch that Tudor manufactures. Hence, the North Flag. And if for some reason the MT 5621 has a limited production, I will still have the first watch ever to be released with it, the North Flag. At the same time, I have my Ranger, solid, reliable, beautiful in its simplicity and renowned reliability. The best of both worlds... Once I get my North Flag, which, unfortunately will be some time out due to limited watch funds, it will be interesting to see which watch gets more wrist time. More to follow!.....

title: Aren't "microspheres" a kind of microbead? Not good!
text:
It's thick but absorbs quickly and has a light, pleasant scent.
However, in another of the JeNu products, they say they use a "proprietary MicroSphere Conducting Gel."
More than a week ago, I asked (in the Questions section of this page), "Does the 'microsphere technology' use plastic microbeads, which are bad for the environment? If they aren't plastic, what ARE they made of?"
That question has been sadly lingering. I'm no chemist, but from what I've been able to determine with a little Internet research, "microspheres" actually ARE a kind of microbead. If that's the case, then this would be among the products that are poisoning lake and ocean life. Microbeads are too small to be filtered out of municipal water systems, and 90% of the high concentration of plastics in the Great Lake has been linked to personal care / cosmetics. Several US states have already passed legislation against use of microbeads, though those laws don't go into effect for a few more years yet.
I'll hang on to this product while awaiting a more definitive answer. However, until I can be convinced that these "microspheres" are not actually plastics that are harming the environment, I will do with this as with other "microbead" products: seal it in a plastic bag and send it to the landfill. (Obviously, "flushing" it away would add to the problem!)
I used this eye cream for several days without problems, albeit without the wand, since I also looked into the "ultrasound" technology, which works by creating minuscule tears in the tissue, which the body then heals, and I'm not sure that's a great beauty solution for the long term.
If I find that I'm wrong in my assessments, I'll be more than happy to update my review.

Purified Water (Aqua), Glycerin, Isocetyl Stearate, Butylene Glycol, Palmitoyl Oligopeptide, Palmitoyl Tetrapeptide -7, Stearic Acid, Stearyl Alchohol, Sodium Lauryl Sulfate, Triethanolamine, Cetyl Alcohol, Glyceryl Stearate, Phenoxyethanol, Squalane, Carbomer, Allantoin, Tocopherol, Acetate, Polysorbate 20, Jojoba (Buxus Chinensis) Oil, Retinyl Palmitate, fragrance, Trisodium EDTA, Butylparaben, Ethylparaben, Imidazolidinyl Urea, Isobutylparaben, Propylparaben, Methylparaben
I want to review each ingredient ;
Glycerin is a good re hydrant which helps in moisturizing skin. It is a natural cooling liquid which soothes our skin. Glycerin has many applications for the skin and hair Glycerin can be used in many ways. It can be mixed with other natural substances to provide maximum benefits to your skin. Glycerin makes an excellent toner when mixed with rosewater. Lemon and glycerin cleanser also helps to remove the dirt from the skin. Glycerin can be used directly on the skin as well. Glycerin is beneficial for the skin Also called glycerol or glycerine, glycerin is present in all natural lipids (fats), whether animal or vegetable. It can be derived from natural substances by hydrolysis of fats and by fermentation of sugars; it also can be synthetically manufactured. Glycerin is a skin-identical and skin-repairing ingredient, meaning it is a substance found naturally in skin. In that respect it is one of the many substances in skin that help maintain the outer barrier and prevent dryness or scaling.

Isocetyl Stearate is the ester of Isocetyl Alcohol and Stearic Acid (found in animal and vegetable fats) and acts primarily as a lubricant on the skin's surface. It dries to form a thin coating, giving the skin a soft and smooth appearance , acts as a lubricant

BUTYLENE GLYCOL: Butylene glycol (1.3-Butanediol) is a small organic alcohol used as solvent and conditioning agent.
Function(s): Fragrance Ingredient; Skin-Conditioning Agent - Miscellaneous; Solvent; ViscosityDecreasing Agent; HUMECTANT; MASKING; SKIN CONDITIONING; VISCOSITY CONTROLLING

palmitoyl oligopeptide a blend of palmitic acid (a fatty acid) with several amino acids, including alanine, arginine, aspartic acid, glycine, histidine, lysine, proline, serine and/or valine. peptides have cell-communicating ability and can help skin cells function in a more normal, healthy manner. formulary protocols need to be followed to ensure the peptide remains stable during use, it is also possible that Palmitoyl oligopeptide may stimulate collagen production and encourage the production of intercellular matrix substances such as hyaluronic acids. The current regulatory name for this peptide is now palmitoyl hexapeptide-12.
Palmitoyl Tetrapeptide-7/ also known as Matrixyl 3000 is a synthetic peptide comprised of four amino acids that is used in beauty products and cosmetics to suppress the production of excess interleukins, the chemical messengers which trigger the body’s acute inflammatory response. This can lead to glycation damage, or the process by which glucose links with proteins and causes them to bind together, stiffening tissues. This negatively affects the skin's support system, comprised of collagen, elastin and other proteins, and leads to wrinkles, sagging, and uneven skin tone
Stearyl Alcohol is a naturaly fatty alcohol derived from stearic acid, coconut oil or vegetable fatty acids, and is used to soothe and soften as a conditioning agent and as an emulsifier. It is often found as a hair coating ingredient in shampoos and conditioners, and an emollient in creams and lotions for the skin . It can also be used to thicken formulas, adding body and viscosity.
Stearyl Alcohol is FDA and CIR approved.
SLS is the sodium salt of lauryl sulfate, and is classified by the EWG Cosmetics Database as a "denaturant, surfactant cleansing agent, emulsifier and foamer, I would suggest going to websites and reading about sodium laurel sulfates , there is a lot of information about them, and potential negative effects, studies that have been done regarding this ingredient in shampoos, and other products
Triethanolamine, often abbreviated as TEA, is a viscous organic compound,serves as a pH balancer
Cetyl alcohol was discovered in 1817 by the French chemist Michel Chevreul when he heated spermaceti, a waxy substance obtained from sperm whale oil, with caustic potash (potassium hydroxide). Flak Cetyl alcohol is used in the cosmetic industry as an opacifier in shampoos, or as an emollient, emulsifier or thickening agent in the manufacture of skin creams and lotions. usually obtained from palm oil.
Glyceryl stearate is created by the esterification of glycerin and stearic acid. Glyceryl stearate creates an excellent emulsion and when used in combination with other emulsifiers, creates a stable lotion, ability to make the oils which are combined in the emulsion non greasy.
Phenoxyethanol is usually synthesized for commercial use but it can also be found naturally in products such as green tea. - is an oily, slightly sticky liquid with a faint rose-like scent. It is used as a preservative in a wide variety of cosmetic and personal care products.
Squalene is a natural 30-carbon organic compound originally obtained for commercial purposes primarily from shark liver oil (hence its name), although plant sources (primarily vegetable oils) are now used as well, including amaranth seed, rice bran, wheat germ, and olives. It is also found in high concentrations in the stomach oil of birds in the order Procellariiformes. All plants and animals produce squalene as a biochemical intermediate, including humans, Squalene is one of the most common lipids produced by human skin cells. It is a natural moisturizer.
Possible health benefits
It has been suspected that sharks are resistant to cancer due to high tissue levels of squalene., Squalene anti-tumor activity in animal experiments and epidemiological evidence based on olive oil consumption also suggest reduction of cancer risk by squalene
Squalene is a hydrocarbon and a triterpene, and is a natural and vital part of the synthesis of all plant and animal sterols, including cholesterol, steroid hormones and vitamin D in the human body.
The Carbomers chemical synthetic help to distribute or suspend an insoluble solid in a liquid. They are also used to keep emulsions from separating into their oil and liquid components. Carbomers are often used to control the consistency and flow of cosmetics and personal care products, water-absorbing compounds.
The function of a carbomer is to act as an emulsion stabilizer and to adjust viscosity and can therefore also be classed as a thickening agent.
Allantoin is present in botanical extracts of the comfrey plant and in the urine of most mammals. Chemically synthesized bulk allantoin, which is chemically equivalent to natural allantoin, is safe, non-toxic, compatible with cosmetic raw materials and meets CTFA and JSCI requirements,
Manufacturers cite several beneficial effects for allantoin as an active ingredient in over-the-counter cosmetics, including: a moisturizing and keratolytic effect, increasing the water content of the extracellular matrix and enhancing the desquamation of upper layers of dead skin cells, increasing the smoothness of the skin; promoting cell proliferation and wound healing; and a soothing, anti-irritant, and skin protectant effect by forming complexes with irritant and sensitizing agents.
A animal study in 2010 found that based on the results from histological analyses, a soft lotion with 5% allantoin ameliorates the wound healing process, by modulating the inflammatory response. The study also suggests that quantitative analysis lends support to the idea that allantoin also promotes fibroblast proliferation and synthesis of the extracellular matrix.
Tocopherol is vitamin E, benefits of vitamin E: it seals in moisture, softens and hydrates skin, the next ingredient listed is acetate, Tocopheryl acetate is often added to skin creams and other cosmetic products in order to make them last longer during shipping, storage.
Polysorbate 20 used as a wetting agent usually polysorbate is a harmless sorbitol, which is a sugar alcohol.
For its use in personal care products, research says it’s treated with ethylene oxide—thus, the name “polysorbate 20,” because it’s treated with 20 parts of ethylene oxide. I do not know much about this ingredient, please do your own research, this is information I found and there is more information on this ingredient found in many personal care products.
SIMMONDSIA CHINENSIS (JOJOBA) SEED OIL: Jojoba oil is extracted from seeds of the desert shrub, Simmondsia chinensis, native to California, Arizona and Mexico. function(s): Hair Conditioning Agent; Skin-Conditioning Agent - Occlusive; EMOLLIENT; SKIN CONDITIONING.
Retinyl palmitate is the the ester of retinol (vitamin A) combined with palmitic acid, a saturated fatty acid and a major component of palm oil. It is not considered to be the same ingredient as retinol, although it is converted to retinol, and then to the active component of retinoic acid once it is absorbed by the skin after being topically applied. It belongs to the family of chemical compounds known as retinoids and is one of the most important vitamins for the appearance of the skin because of its small molecular structures. These tiny molecules have the ability to penetrate the outer layers of the skin and work to repair the lower layers where collagen and elastin reside
Retinyl palmitate is considered a less irritating form of retinol, and a gentler ingredient on sensitive skin. However, the reason retinyl palmitate may cause less irritation is because of the lengthier process that must take place for it to be converted into retinoic acid (otherwise known as tretinoin), the active compound that creates the cell regeneration and exfoliation action within the skin.
Retinyl palmitate converts into retinol (or vitamin A), which in turn is converted into retinoic acid by specialized enzymes in the skin. Retinoic acid facilitates communication between cells, encouraging aging cells to continue their renewal process, and regenerate collagen and elastin to prevent the appearance of aging skin, wrinkles, and fine lines. It is also effective at producing new, healthy skin cells to replace skin previously damaged by acne (However, retinol cannot communicate with a cell until it has been broken down into retinoic acid . Once this breakdown has occurred, communication begins and the cells' turnover rate increases, thus speeding up the production of collagen.Retinyl palmitate is considered an exfoliator (albeit more gentle than pure retinol), and its effect of repeatedly shedding the upper dermal layer forces the skin to produce new cells.
Squalene is used in cosmetics, and more recently as an immunologic adjuvant in vaccines. Squalene has been proposed to be an important part of the Mediterranean diet as it may be a chemopreventive substance that protects people from cancer.
About TRISODIUM EDTA: EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid) is a chelating agent, used to sequester and decrease the reactivity of metal ions that may be present in a product.
BUTYLPARABEN: Butylparaben is in the paraben family of preservatives used by the food, pharmaceutical, and personal care product industries. Parabens mimic estrogen and can act as potential hormone (endocrine) system disruptors.Function(s): Fragrance Ingredient; Preservative; MASKING
Ethylparaben is in the paraben family of preservatives used by the food, pharmaceutical, and personal care product industries. Parabens mimic estrogen and can act as potential hormone (endocrine) system disruptors. Function(s): Fragrance Ingredient; Preservative

IMIDAZOLIDINYL UREA (FORMALDEHYDE RELEASER): Imidazolidinyl urea is an antimicrobial preservative that works by forming formaldehyde in cosmetic products. People exposed to such formaldehyde-releasing ingredients may develop a formaldehyde allergy or an allergy to the ingredient itself. In the U.S. approximately 20% of cosmetics and personal care products contain a formaldehyde-releaser and the frequency of contact allergy to these ingredients is much higher among Americans compared to studies in Europe.
This ingredient may be derived from animals. From PETA's Caring Consumer: Excreted from urine and other bodily fluids. In deodorants, ammoniated dentifrices, mouthwashes, hair colorings, hand creams, lotions, shampoos, etc. Used to "brown" baked goods, such as pretzels. Derivatives: Imidazolidinyl Urea, Uric Acid. Alternatives: synthetics.
Isobutylparaben is in the parabens family of preservatives used by the food, pharmaceutical, and personal care product industries. research this ingredient to learn more
Propylparaben is in the paraben family of preservatives used by the food, pharmaceutical, and personal care product industries. Parabens mimic estrogen and can act as potential hormone (endocrine) system disruptors. Function(s): Fragrance Ingredient; Preservative; PERFUMING
METHYLPARABEN: Methylparaben is in the paraben family of preservatives used by the food, pharmaceutical, and personal care product industries. Parabens mimic estrogen and can act as potential hormone (endocrine) system disruptors, Fragrance Ingredient; Preservative

I finally ordered the Xtava 2200 from a daily deal site and it fits perfectly. Totally worth the hassle of buying a new dryer to be able to use the Orchid.

The hype is true. This thing works.

Here's what I do for my curls. I use Deva no-poo and then Deva one condition in the shower. I don't rinse it out. After I get out of the shower, add Deva curling gel, flip head over, scoop and squeeze with microfiber towel. Hair should feel like seaweed consistency. Then lean hair onto the orchid diffuser and don't touch it. Scoop up big amounts into the orchid while leaning forward or back. When it's all dry, use fingers to get it un-crunchy. Done! You can even reactivate with water on the hairline for several days.

Once you've got a dryer it fits on, the Orchid is a curly girl's best friend.

text: I actually purchased this kit from Walgreens and followed the instructions to a T. My nails ended up looking terrible and bumpy after the 1st nail was complete. I messaged Kiss Products via facebook and received a a response from them immediately. I asked the rep if there was a secret to using the product and how weird it was that the product turned out the way it did, What they told me is to apply the gel one nail at a time and move on to the next nail since the gel cannot dry while waiting for the activator. In the instructions it says to do all nails on one hand with gel then apply activator. They ended up sending me a replacement kit and this time i followed the tips they gave me. My nails came out looking great through out the whole process.However, when it came to apply the final layer of gel on top of the activator (per the instructions, I only applied the gel over wet activator on one nail) I noticed my gel brush was gradually getting harder and by the last nail was hard as a rock. I suggest waiting for the final layer of gel/activator to dry then adding the final layer of gel to get the gel like shine.

text:
Bought at a big box store, but have used it for about a year now and have decided to shop for a new trimmer. At first, with just a short goatee to trim, it performed admirably. Now, with a full beard that I keep trimmed, it cannot cleanly keep it trimmed. It misses large swaths of hair, pulls hairs badly, and generally doesn't have a clean, sharp cut. title: main ingredients are water and alcohol - not aloe.
text:
The first two ingredients in this product's long list are water and denatured alcohol. Aloe is number seven. It is described, however, as an "aloe gel" and recommended for soothing a sunburn. I wish I had read the ingredient list before I bought, because I can't imagine trying to sooth a sunburn with denatured alcohol. I had a slight sunburn when I put this stuff on my face, and it did feel cool, but with a slight sting. Alcohol feels cool on the skin, and since there is a lot more alcohol than aloe in this product I suspect alcohol is what caused the cooling effect, as well as the sting.
The cooling effect passed quickly, and the gel was not absorbed by my skin - it dried to a thick paste that now felt warm instead of cool. I can't imagine it as a makeup base any more than as a soothing sunburn treatment. The most enjoyable part of my experience was washing it off.
This stuff, however, does score an easy 5 stars for visuals. The glass jar is lovely, and the gel is also - thick and clear - it does look cool.

title: Absolutely works for me.
text:
My big toenail was curving so much that the nail ends were almost parallel to each other. One side was bleeding and I started to put strips of cotton to stop the nail from digging into my skin. After a few failed attempts to properly install curvecorrect strips, I got it right and almost immediately felt relief. A few days later after the open wound healed, I knew this product was a winner. I went through the entire pack of strips and my big toe nail had not caused any issues. After about 7 months or so of not wearing it, my nail seemed to be curving again, so I ordered another kit to help maintain a straighter nail.

Some tips I learned on application:
-Make sure your nail is relatively free of large ridges - sand those ridges down. I also like to lightly scuff the strip where the glue will be for better adhesion.
-Prep both surfaces well - wipe the nail and strip down with solvent to ensure there are no dust or oil remnants. Make sure the nail and strip are dry before application.
-The amount of adhesive needed is very minimal. I like to apply a drop onto the strip, then lightly smear the glue with a file edge (or piece of paper) to ensure that there is not too much glue.
-Follow the included directions and use the back of the cotton swab to hold down the strip while the glue is being cured to your nail. I found that if I moved at all during this step, where the strip was allowed to move once it touched my nail, that the adhesion was not very good.

title: Omg! I had been looking for something like this forever!
text:
I’m a beauty blender fan for makeup application, but am also a germophobe (and have autoimmune issues) and clean my brushes after every application. I’d tried various things for drying my blenders out after washing and for storing so they stay clean, but nothing was functional with my routine, bathroom, etc....
So when I heard about these and finally found some for sale, I couldn’t bring myself to pay more for the holder than I did my blender, so I just passed. I was sad, but lo and behold, I came across this and couldn’t hit “add to cart” fast enough!
They do exactly what you want them to do; keep your beauty blender upright in a vented holder to dry out and remain for your next use so that you know you’re using a clean “brush” every time. They also help the blenders keep their shape and I’ve noticed my current BB’s are outlasting any others I’ve had because of these stands. Usually, they will start to crack in the middle making it where they absorb too much product and useless. I think it’s because of my cleaning and then having to ring them out so much and store them together in containers that were smashing them.
Not anymore! Oh and if you’re leery about having them take up countertop space, don’t . You obviously don’t have to leave them out, but if you choose to, they look very classy and are very “in” with the different geometric shapes made of “gold”.

They really are adorable and I think add more than function to your bathroom; they also add style. You get 3 similar sized holders, but they aren’t the exact same which is great for your different sized/brands of blenders. Every brand I own fit perfectly even when fully “swollen” with moisture.
As you can see from the pics, they are wide enough to hold even your minis together but still know they have ample breathing room to dry out. And please disregard my dirty blenders since I just finished using them and haven’t cleaned them yet ;)

title: My favorite cleaner but please read!
text:
So as I stated in the description this is my absolute favorite cleaner to keep pores clean and breakout free. I have been using this for a couple of months now. (I have bought from a local drugstore and not on amazon) however there are some things I need to explain.

The main active ingredient (what makes it clean so well) is charcoal. Now I personally love just about any cleaner I've used that includes charcoal but there are a few things you should keep in mind if you've never used a charcoal based cleanser.
1. Charcoal does deep clean and can cause a tingling/ irritation on your skin so if you have extremely sensitive skin please try a small area first before covering your entire face.
2. I ALWAYS use a moisturizer after using this as it can make your skin somewhat dry due to cleaning out all of the oil and gunk from your pores.
3. Breakouts the first couple of times you use this is not necessarily a bad thing since your skin has to purge (get rid of all of the gunk that has built up under your skin surface for longer than you probably realize), if this persists I would definately consider changing up something but some pimples or breakouts are not necessarily bad just give it a chance.
4. I only use this cleaner at most 3 times a week to avoid over drying but use moisturizer every night.

I do believe I covered everything I was wanting to. If you have breakouts on your body I have used it for that also. If I could I would use this everyday because I love how glowing and clean my face looks after using it. Everyone's skin is different so even though I can't use daily you may notice you can just please note the things I addressed above.
If this review was helpful to you please click yes so that it may be easier to be found and be able to help others as well.

In fact, I went out without gloves a few weeks back and forgot to put sunscreen on my hands. I was only out for 90 minutes and my hands got burnt pretty baldly- to the point that they peeled later. So yes, I can confidently say that this product is working.

It goes on easily without feeling greasy. Your skin will look a little shiny, but nothing extreme. It has a nice smell to it. It doesn't burn my eyes. I'm not sure what more you could want besides a lower price, but it's a great product and worth a little extra.

Then I saw this Amazon ad for the "RQ12Pro" replacement head. I was hoping it was a new iteration of the replacement head, improving on the widely panned RQ12+. At this point, I'm still not sure if that is true, or if it is just a different name for the RQ12+. Googling "RQ12pro" yields very few results, most of them in Polish.

I ordered it anyhow. And I was very pleasantly surprised. The box does indeed say "RQ12pro". Like the RQ12+, this RQ12pro does not flip open to clean; rather, you need to pry off the cutters, rinse them separately, leave them on the counter to dry, then reattach them when ready to shave again. That's not quite as convenient as the original RQ12, but really no big deal. My review is based entirely on the quality of the shave.

I just had my first shave with this and it gets a big thumbs up! Mowed through 4 days of stubble without any trouble, and left me ultra-smooth, even around the chin and neck. I can't provide a fair side-by-side comparison with the RQ12 because mine is past its prime. But based on my memory of how the RQ12 worked when it was new, this one is just as good if not better. I have no idea if the RQ12pro is a renamed RQ12+ or an improved version. Regardless, I am very happy with it.

title: Absolutely works!
text:
Came in a couple days and I immediately used it to do some stamp nail art.

I've used stampers similar to these, not sure if they were the Born Pretty brand though. Using stampers can be difficult for beginners. It takes some time to learn the proper techniques to stamp correctly and even to swipe the nail polish off the plate. Here are some tips to make sure you are stamping correctly if it doesn't seem to be working, because these stampers do work!

1) On a stamping plate, only cover part of the design you want with polish, about half. Try to use thicker/more pigmented polishes.
2) Scrape at a low angle, not completely vertically. Sweep the polish off the plate in one quick motion. Try not to scrape multiple times.
3) Roll the stamp across the plate quickly and in one motion to pick up the polish
4) Within a few seconds, place the stamp over the section of nail you want using the clear design of the stamp
5) Again, roll the stamp over the nail and be sure to get the top and sides of the nails
6) Use something sticky like tape or a lint roller to remove the excess nail polish. DO NOT use nail polish remover

DO NOT BUFF the stampers. These are clear stampers and do not need buffing! When I used the stampers immediately after receiving them, I did not buff them and they worked fine.
These stamps come slightly sticky, do not clean them, and store them with the tops on when not in use. My favorite part of these stamps is actually the tops because I've had stampers tear while traveling because I didn't have tops to cover them.
Be gentle when ever pressing onto a stamping plate or a nail, if you are too rough they will eventually split and your stamping designs will have strange holes in them. I allowed my sister to borrow my previous stamper to try out some stamping and she brutalized the jelly applicator, hence why I needed new ones and bought these.
I already had some scrapers, so I didn't use the ones that came with these yet. If you don't like these scrapers, maybe because they are too small or too flimsy, then try using an old credit/gift card.

title: Updated Model is Awesome
text:
I would give it 4.5 stars if I could, but 5 will do for now. Will revise if I run into problems down the road, like if the unit dies within a year.

I bought this bcause of the protection that the UL rating implies, and because it has low EMF. These things indicated that the people who made the product care about the health of their customers, and or know that their educated customers will be looking for these features.

This product seems to have been updated, the controller is different now and my guess is that the old version of this model's controller was where the issue was cropping up for former customers who have complained on here. Since I've brought up the controller I'll talk a little bit about it now.

It's simple, nothing complicated here. There are two buttons on the left for controlling heat level from levels 1 (L) - 10 (H), in the manual you will see that the numbers corrospond to specific heat ranges, that's something you will have to memorize or make a note and keep near the controller if that is important to you. The range is: 98.6 F - 140 F. Whenever you turn on the unit, the setting will revert to H (10) or 140F. You do have to decrease the temperature manually to lower it. I personally find 3 or 5 comfortable. H is great for the really cold and bitter nights, or perhaps if you're using it for it's designed purpose warming up your patients.

In the manual it states that a person must be lying or sitting on it for it to work. This means you can't pre-heat it, which makes the default H (10) setting at 10 hours understandable. For a massage therapist this product would be awesome. You can turn it on, leave it on for the full work day (I don't think any massage therapist can do more than 9 hours in a day) and it will heat only when your clients are on the table. As a person who is using this for my bed, I feel fortunate that this can go for 10 hours like a bed mattresses can, most other massage table warmers can only go up to 3 or 4 hours, maybe 6. I tend to set it for 2 or 3 hours at a comfortable level (usually level L) when sleeping since it is better for the body for the temperature to drop during the night. Sometimes I'll run it for 10 hours at the lowest setting L if I am particularly cold.

The controller is about 2 sheets of paper (long side) away from the pad, and 5 sheets of paper from the plug, so the cord is about 7 & 1/2 sheets of paper long or 3 yards/ meters. Some people may need an extension cord, but I think this will be fine for most situations.

The back lighting of the led screen is a very bright blue, this is probably the biggest thing I would like to change, blue disrupts melatonin production which is what is responsible for creating that tired "I'm ready for sleep" feeling. In a massage therapy setting with the light on, it's not a big deal. But for me as a person who turns this on in the dark just before sleeping this is an annoyance. The backlight stays on for about 15 seconds after the last keypress. For people interested in learning more about circadian rhythms and blue light have a read at blue light filtering software - Flux's website, click on the Research page. Sorry I can't give a direct link, external websitss get censored on this website.

At first glance the controller looks upside down, but actually it's very comfortable and conveniently placed so that the therapist can grab it and "pick it up" from the higher half, then when picking up the arm, the lower half with the lcd display becomes the higher half. The product has had careful considerations put into it's design, it is designed for humans :).

I've been pretty happy with my master massage table warmer. I hope some of you looking for a product like this will give this one a try, I'm certainly satisfied.

I've had the product for about a month now, and it is perfect for my use. I use it as a "mattress pad". Why get this over a real matress pad? Well I don't sleep on a matress. I sleep on two closed cell foam pads stacked on top of each other. This pad is about two hand widths wider than my bed, a matress pad for a twin sized bed would be even bigger and waste more electricity. Electricity savings was the reason I was looking at matress pads then massage table warmers versus electric blankets which half their heat just floats up to the ceiling totally wasted. Which brings me to the next feature.

It seems that the mat will only heat up the areas that have weight on them. Some people will like this feature in favor of energy savings and efficiency, others want more even heating (I'm thinking shins). So, the surface you have beneath the table warmer can make a difference some tables are stiff and somewhat convex (less heat) versus maybe if you had a memory foam layer beneath (make sure it's fire retardant!) everything would get heated pretty well. I honestly have not noticed this until I did this in-depth review and my closed cell foam pads are pretty firm and stiff (but flat, neither concave nor convex, or rather both on a micro scale that kinda cancels each other out!). I'm usually warm enough with the heat stored with my faux down comforter on top of me. So, again, considering most massage patients will be only covered in a sheet/wrap the H default setting makes sense.

The texture is a comfortable fleece, I like it a lot, but seeing as it's white you will definitely want to cover it with something (waterproof recommended) to avoid having to wash it. It says it is machine washable on the tin, but I think that's going to shorten the lifespan (if it doesn't outright break the thing) of this product.

I think that's about all I have for this review for now. I will update on longevity when the time comes.

Disclosure: I am not affiliated with the company, I bought his product with my own money and have had no contact with employees of Master Massage. I am making this review as a consumer that prefers high quality products that bring value to my life. I don't buy things just to have things, they must be functional and improve my life.

If you have any questions please ask,

Regards,

Adam

title: Reason to be skeptical
text:
As a curly-haired archaeologist with a specialty in ethnobotany, I so wanted to give this a try. The incredible marula tree is widely used across Africa for its tasty and highly nutritious fruit (more Vitamin C than citrus), nutritious seeds, and an edible oil that is also widely used in cosmetics. The oil has a long shelf life and thus reduces the need for other preservatives (like parabens). And it is harvested by women (who I hope are getting fair pay) without damaging the trees. That sustains the natural environment much better than growing coffee or chocolate or cut flowers, which are other cash crops in Africa and require cutting down forests.

So I wanted to try it and support a company that is widening the market for a woman-produced natural product. But then I read the description and ingredients. Be skeptical. Be very, very skeptical.

The description says marula is "a rich oil harvested for 12,000 years in Madagascar." This may be just a typo, but humans arrived in Madagascar around 1,200 years ago (as far as we know yet). Also, is Sclerocarya birrea (marula) "native to Madagascar," as in the description? Well, sort of. It's native to a large swath of southern Africa and apparently was introduced to Madagascar after people arrived but before recorded history. Maybe that's close enough.

As for ingredients, the company says that "Marula Oil Is one of the purest used on hair today," and that the product is "packed with Marula." I don't know how marula oil could be "purer" than, say, olive or coconut or almond or jojoba oil, but okay, it's pure. What about the purity of the eleven ingredients listed before it, starting with water and including such things as Behentrimonium Chloride, Glyceryl Stearate, PEG-100 Stearate, Stearamidopropyl Dimethylamine, Propanediol, Hydrogenated Ethylhexyl Olivate, Amodimethicone, and (guess what!) jojoba oil? In other words, there are more of those ingredients than marula oil. Note also that amodimethicone is a silicone, which is inexpensive and coats the hair, so in the short term it tames frizz, but in the long term it often makes hair dry and brittle.

Bottom line: If you have good results with silicone-based products (e.g., Frizz-Ease) and jojoba oil, and try to avoid paraben-based preservatives for health and ecological reasons, and don't mind the smell of rose oil, you'll probably like this hair cream. Just consider whether you're actually paying for (and applying to your hair) much marula oil compared to a whole bunch of other ingredients.

title: Healthy alternative to relaxers. THE BEST!!!
text:
I don't know where to start, because I have So much to say.

But first of all, it is IMPORTANT TO READ THE TIPS BELOW BEFORE STARTING YOUR AT-HOME TREATMENT. Some important steps and tips were omitted in the instructions.

I am rating this on its performance because in the end, that is what matters. And since this company is out to make its customers happy, I am confident that they will update their instructions.

If you have unruly, dry or unmanageable hair, this is a MUST TRY for you. Even if you'd just like to make you hair a bit more manageable or to have to spend less time doing your hair each day - this is an absolutely wonderful product to do just that.

This Amazonliss Keratin Treatment has literally changed my hair-care life, which in turn, of course, changes my entire life. I now spend so much less time doing my hair, and can now spend more time doing things that I love.

I used to have what I'd call in-between hair. Not soft or easy, but not terribly hard. My hair was between curly and wavy, quite frizzy, and quite unmanageable. I wouldn't say totally unmanageable, but I'd have to work VERY hard and VERY long, just to get OK results. It would take me about an hour to blow-dry my hair, and at the end, my arms were so weak, I had no more energy to work on it any longer. I'm not sure whether my hair was better before the blowouts or after. I would always wear my hair up in a bun, tied up as much as possible, in order to look neat. Nothing I tried was good enough. I had done some relaxings before. However I didn't like the idea of using such harsh chemicals in my hair. It also made my hair feel unnaturally thick. It also costs a lot, and doing it at home is very, very hard.

I was excited to try this Amazonliss Keratin Trearment. It's more natural which is a lot better for the hair and body. And having done an at-home relaxing, I must say it is A WHOLE LOT EASIER to do on your own than a relaxer.

I will break the instructions down below, but for now I'll tell you how I did it. I've done a lot of research before starting. I wanted to get it right and I want you to get it right too.

I washed my hair twice with the shampoo. Then I allowed it to air dry a bit to make blow-drying easier. Then I blow-dried my hair on medium heat. Using gloves and in a well-ventilated area, I applied the treatment in sections, around 1" of hair at a time. I used my gloved finger to apply it to my hair at the roots, then smoothed it down, and finished by combing through to ensure the treatment reached all over. When I completed all the hair, I put a bit extra in my problem areas; which for me are around the hairline at the forehead and neck.

Then I let the treatment sit in my hair for around 1/2 hr. I allowed it to dry a bit, then dried it totally with the blow dryer on cool air. It took quite some time to get it all dry.

I then ironed my hair in the same way I applied the treatment. I sectioned my hair and ironed about an inch at a time. For me it was easier to hold the chunk of hair taut at a 90 degree angle, while going over from the root to middle 10 times. I then ironed from the middle down about 5 times.

An important step that was omitted in the instructions was that you're not supposed to wash your hair out for 3 days. I left it in and re-ironed any messed-up areas during the three days. My hair felt quite good throughout this time.

When the three days were up, I rinsed my hair. I then towel dried it so it wouldn't be dripping-wet, then I applied the mask generously through my hair. I worked it in to ensure every inch was covered. I covered my hair with a shower cap to seal in the moisture and left it in for 1/2 hour. I then rinsed it out well and waited to see results.

And see results I did!

My oh my, are the results fabulous!!!

My hair dried naturally straight on top, and wavy on the bottom. And oh so smooth!!

I then blow-dried my hair. I must tell you, it's a world of a difference to blow-dry hair after this keratin treatment as opposed to before. The hair dries a lot faster, it is easier to work with the hair (section, brush), and the results... The results are fabulous!!!

Until now, it took me about an hour to dry my hair, without even getting great results. Now it took me just 20 minutes!!! And the results are indescribable!!

My hair is silky smooth, lusciously bouncy, and I was surprised to see that it has even made my natural highlights strike out so beautifully!!

I am so proud of my hair now, I'm bouncing it around all day. My hair feels healthy. Nourished. Smooth. I know, I can't say SMOOTH often enough. Because it's indescribable.

Now, you might be wary of the fact that this treatment requires so much heat. But in the long run, you won't need half as much heat on your hair as before. Now that's something to think about!

Now, to break down the instructions and tips for you:

STEPS:
*** WORK IN A WELL-VENTILATED AREA***
1) wash hair twice using the step 1 shampoo.
2) allow to air-dry a bit for easier blowout, then blow-dry your hair until it's mostly done.
3) put on gloves.
4) section your hair to your convenience. I find it's the easiest to section in 4, then section further as needed
5) apply treatment to small areas at a time; smooth out and comb through.
6) leave in for 20 minutes.
7) allow to air-dry a bit, then dry your hair with a blower on COOL setting. Drying it on hot will not give you good results.
8) section hair again as before. Iron about 1" of hair at a time. Iron at a 90 degree angle to ensure a straight root. Iron 8-10 times from root to middle, then 4-6 times from middle to end. This process burns the treatment into the hair. So however it's done now, is how the treatment will stay in your hair.
9) don't wash your hair before 3 days. And don't tie your hair up. Leave it down. Re-iron as needed throughout the three days.
10) after three days, rinse hair well
11) towel dry so your hair isn't dripping-wet. Apply mask. Wrap your hair in a shower cap. Leave in for 20-30 minutes.
12) rinse hair well
13) style as desired

AND ENJOY YOUR NATURALLY BEAUTIFUL HAIR!

Tips:
**All keratin treatments have a VERY sharp smell. This smell isn't necessarily bad. I didn't mind the actual scent. But it's SO sharp. So work in a very well-ventilated area. Also, when blow-drying or ironing your hair during the treatment process, blow or iron away from your face because the fumes can make your eyes sting a lot.
**Towel drying hair before applying mask helps the mask to absorb better in the hair.
**if you have extremely thick or very long or very full hair, you may need more than one pack. The treatment had just about enough for my full, past shoulder-length hair. Just to be on the safe side, apply less on the bottom, so you can ration proportionately when you get the the end/top. You can always go back and apply more as needed. But you can't take off.
** this takes quite some time. I think it took me about 3 hours. It will depend on your type as well as amount of hair. So schedule this at a time when you're not rushed. The results will last a few months, so you may as well do it right.

I will update if I have any changes or want to add more tips.

I am so in love with my new hair. I am sure you will too. Your hair will thank you.

I do my best to help potential buyers. Especially when it comes to beauty :) I believe all women should be empowered to beautify themselves on their own. If my review was of help, kindly vote yes and/or ask any questions! I'd be happy to help!

Although I received this at a discount for testing purposes, this review is my own and reflect my honest opinions. I am loving this product!!

I will typically use a guide if I am going for a precise wing, but using tape or another flat edge disrupts my base makeup or eye look and defeats the purpose of precision. The winged eyeliner stamps were really quick to apply, relatively easy to touch up and the liner dried almost instantly so no smudging occurred.

The only potential drawbacks are that the liner itself is a rather thick felt tip. It's easy to draw on quickly, but I wasn't able to get a very fine point on my wings as a result. However, I could always use a fine brush tip liner to achieve the result I want so this isn't a major issue. The primary time-saver is the fact that the majority of your work is done in an instant.

title: Might be okay for some depending how thick and how often you shave.
text:
Got the package opened it up and first thing is it's all packed very well and safe which I was happy to see. Not crammed into the box.
Pulled it all out and I was shocked to find how light the actual shaver assembly was. I mean it's awesome. This probably comes from the newer type batteries they use.

Anyway let it charge for a bit(as instructions say) and went to use. When you first turn it on the blades make an odd sound for a split second and it has a little jump but once it's going it's fairly quiet.

It "feels" powerful but not in a vibration type way, hard to explain but it's good.
Anyway did my first shave with it and must say I was not too pleased with the results.

I tried different areas in Low, Med, and High and noticed no difference beyond the heat of the blades. It seemed on high that got a bit more warm (friction of metal will do that hah) but didn't notice any difference in cutting.

I've not shaved in 2 days so that may have contributed but still, my old shaver could handle it better. This one I had to pass over the same spots soo many times. and even in spots where like just 1 random hair remained I had trouble sometimes getting it to pick that hair up and chop it.

I stopped and took it apart and cleaned it all and tried to finished (wanted to make sure wasn't full/clogged of hair). Same results.
I think one issue is they have soo many little holes and cuts etc. in the blades that it can't handle as much as my older style which had less but larger cut outs.

That said, this probably will work fine if you keep your face shaved daily and don't have thick hairs. I like to shave every other day generally myself but now find I may have to change that.

The smaller more cut outs on the blades I assume are to help it align hair better to cut etc. but I guess I found that downfall if you go a day without a shave or have suborn hair it might not work as well.

I'll give it some more time. This was only the first time and I'll try to change my habits too. I think that might help it some but still annoyed that it had troubles getting single random hairs.

My old cheap Norelco shaved decent in all these situations. I think this newer one MIGHT be a tad tad tad closer shave but hard to say.

I don't think this shaver is worth $200 so if you can get it on sale/deal maybe, even if it had worked perfect for me.
I've not tried the cleaning base yet. That's the next part I'm worried about since some have leaks/other issues but I will revise if any issues.
I plan to clean the blades directly more often to avoid wasting as much cleaning solution etc.

text:
This foot file was made with safety and comfort in mind. I've used it on wet and dry feet and it is super comfortable. I usually soak my feet then use a blade to remove hardened skin. I finish off with a foot file. Calluses, while not painful, are very uncomfortable to me and this has been an issue in my life for many years. The Pedi Perfect is excellent for in between pedicures. It has two speeds and is rechargeable. The removal of dead skin can get messy, especially on dry feet, so make sure you do this over a towel or over the bathtub to avoid dust on the floor.

My only minor complaints are that I wish the file was a bit rougher, as my feet are pretty bad as far as calluses go. I will have to see if they make replacement buffs in various textures. I also don't know how long the buffer will last before it needs replacing. I am not sure if this is worth the $50 retail cost. It works well and is safe to use, but the cost of replacements may be an issue for some.

Overall, I am very happy with this. It was not a hassle to use like the Pediegg. The risk of nicking the skin is slim to none. My feet felt very nice after using it.

Pretty expensive for a set of eyelid tapes. Definitely works as promised.  Lasts all day and night, if necessary.  Is practically unnoticeable unless you look down, and then it only shows a crease. Placement has to be practiced a couple of times to achieve desired result, but is otherwise reliable.  The only issue I have with it is that it is incredibly difficult to remove; it's really sticky and will leave adhesive on your eyelids if you leave them on there too long.  Everyone says that dabbing water onto it will allow for it to slide off easily, and I think people need to redefine "sliding off easily" because I've tried water, vaseline, and coconut oil, and I still need to gently peel it off in order to remove it, which does cause stretching, which is an issue because it might lead to droopy eyelids.  If anyone finds a good way to actually slide it off, it would be very helpful to note.  On another note, as an Asian with uneven eyelids, I've been trying to match my right eye to my left, doubled-lidded one.  Unfortunately this tape is too thin to pull up my right eyelid into the same deep crease on my right, so if you're looking for a deep crease, this tape won't do it.

title: It used to be GREAT....now it's just better than the alternatives
text:
When I first started using Secret Clinical Strength, I bought a product (numerous times) that was labelled "sensitive" but NOT labelled as "unscented". I recently found an old one I still have kicking around, and sure-enough, on the list of ingredients is a masking fragrance.

I loved, loved, LOVED that deodorant. "Unscented" deodorants always are super smelly. They might not smell like armpit or like flowers, but there is a smell...and whenever I wear them (I've tried numerous brands) it's like the smell haunts me.

So, I was absolutely delighted to find a deodorant that actually didn't smell. Whenever I'd sniff my pits, if I smelled anything at all, it just smelled like me. Not offensively body-odery me...but just a hint of my normal human smell.

Then, I noticed that where that deodorant was previously stocked on the shelf, was now a similar-looking product that was labelled "unscented." Ironically, this newer version has more of a smell to it, which has taken this from being the perfect deodorant to simply being the least-bad option I've found on the market. Additionally, the newer kind has some weird problem with drying out. Even though I use it every day, a crust forms quickly on the top, which clogs the vents through which the deodorant comes up. Dried bits on the surface are abrasive to my underarms, and I spend a silly amount of time trying to unclog the darn thing each morning. (note: at first, I thought maybe I just had a weird one, but I've had the same issue with several of the same product that I've used over the past few months)

It also seems that the wetness protection has diminished...but perhaps my memory is just rosy, or the current weather more challenging.

I'm now looking for a source of the old version to stock up on because I really miss my un-smelly "fragranced" version of the sensitive Secret Clinical Strength deodorant.

title: A good choice for your body and (maybe) you conscience
text:
Let's face it, there are way too many choices out there for washing your body. Sure, you could use a bar of Zest and smell like your grandpa and there's nothing wrong with that... Unless you like dry, itchy skin. But hey, a bar of soap was good enough 200 years ago, so it should still be good today, right?

Sure. And while you're at it, why not ride around on a penny-farthing and wear spats?

But if you're not bound by tradition, you could do a heck of a lot worse than this body wash.

This stuff is pretty great! It uses coconut water instead of boring old regular water! And it has coconut OIL in it.

You ever stop to wonder how a coconut can have oil AND water? I tried to unravel this mystery but I could only find a few coconuts in Murcia before a 'king' came along on some weird 'quest' and took them. But I digress.

Anyway, this stuff won't dry out your skin. That's pretty much the secret to looking young: moisture. And it's priced low enough to make it a great buy, but not so low that the company can't pay fair wages to and buy bicycles for the good people of Togo. So if all that fair trade, bicycle-charity stuff is important to you, you have ANOTHER reason to get this stuff.

PROS:
1. Won't dry out your skin
2. Doesn't smell like artificial coconuts. It smells nice.
3. Pump bottle
4. Bikes for Togoans. Togoites? Togons? Whatever. Togo people.

CONS:
None

And if you see a king with some coconuts (you can tell he's a king because he doesn't have crap all over him) tell him I'm looking for him and I want my coconuts back.

title: Incredible results!
text:
I have always had thin nails that peeled and would never grow past the quick. I have worn acrylic nails for the last 10 years for that reason. When I took them off about 3.5 months ago my nails were bleeding because they had been ground through to the nail bed in places. I received a file like these as a gift shortly thereafter. It seemed to be keeping the damage from worsening so I bought these because I wanted a case (and I lose things so I wanted multiples). Once the damage grew out my nails completely stopped peeling/chipping. They are so thick I can use them to fasten jewelry clasps and peel off labels without any problems. They may not look terribly long in the pic but if you had seen how damaged they were just a few short months ago I think you would be amazed.

I also would like to add my two cents to a couple complaints I have read about this type of file. First, it is much thicker than a regular file and it can be difficult to get under your nails if they are very short. I just filed on the top until they grew out a bit. Second, I saw someone unhappy because of the fine grit. They have a VERY fine grit. If you need to shorten your nails you would need to clip them and then use the file. However, this fine grit is absolutely perfect for me because my nails grow slowly and I want to save as much of them as possible. And finally, a mention of breakage. I have dropped mine several times (on the carpet) and none have broken. Even if I occasionally broke one they would totally be worth the price I paid.

title: It's been two weeks since I started using this consistently
text:
I recently had lumbar spine surgery, so even though the surgery was deemed a success, I still have referred pain from lingering muscle spasms...which I've been told can take up to a year to resolve. So I bought this magnesium oil to help with the spasms. I'm still taking medication, so I do not know if the oil is helping...but getting more magnesium into my system while I'm healing is a good thing. I rub it on my legs, thighs, buttocks and hips. DO NOT PUT THIS ANYWHERE NEAR YOUR INCISION OR IT WILL BURN. I also put some on the soles of my feet, but my feet became too dry...so no more feet. It's essentially a high magnesium salt water...that has a faint scent of low tide...but the smell eventually dissipates. I'm not going to give up on this. I feel using this will give me a long-term benefit on my road to recovery.

one more thing: It does tingle when you apply it...not a pleasant tingling sensation, but a borderline burning sensation. The directions do state that this will happen if you are low in magnesium. I'm at the point where I feel very little, if at all tingling. So don't let the tingle/burn stop you from using it.

title: This was absolutely one of the best purchases EVER!
text:
This has been such a great product for my wife and I!!! We have enjoyed testing out the fragrances we hadn't tried until now; the one's that I have tried went into my desk at work for easy and quick application whenever I'm needing a boost of happiness. This is a perfect and inexpensive way to become acquainted with Penhaligon's, who many consider (myself included) the best perfume house in the world. Do yourself a favor and get this! You deserve a reward for all that hard work, don't you?

The vial sizes are quite large and will give you many days of liberal use. Here's my take on the scents:

Quercus: A very nice, light and woody scent. My wife loves this one on me and I enjoyed it, but wish it was stronger. Smells lemony and a bit floral, with a woody base.
Sartorial: This is my all time favorite of Penhaligon's offerings and the one that got me into their house to begin with. It is a super unique fougere, inspired by the old tailor shops of Saville. It opens with a strong metallic/ozonic scent (the tailor's scissors), that warms into a spicey, floral heart. The bas is my favorite part, having a lingering smell of cedar wood, vanilla and amber. Throughout the scent's life runs a string of bee's wax, used to symbolize the wax a tailor runs their thread through for every stitch. I absolutely love this one and own a large bottle of it!
Blenheim Bouquet: Bright citrus and lavender play a big role in this one's top notes; interestingly, there are no heart notes, but after several hours it transitions to the base notes of musky, piney, peppery goodness. I honestly didn't know what to think of this one at first, but it has grown on me and I love it now. Wearing it, you smell like a proper, British gentleman.
Opus 1870: There is no question on this one's scent: it's all wood! There are supposed to be coriander, pepper and citrus, but those notes are fleeting and typically hidden under the strong scent of oak. This is not my favorite of the bunch, but I do like it.
Endymion: This is such a great scent! Putting it on for the evening makes me feel ready for whatever. The top notes are lavender, bergamot, sage and orange. Those gradually melt into a warm scent of coffee and geranium; this wonderful, warm and uplifting scent lingers for 2-3 hours. Eventually a light, skin-close scent of leather, myrhh, and many various spicy or musky notes that occasionally come through. Every note of this fragrance is sublime and it is my favorite, after Sartorial that is. My only complaint about Endymion is that, much like Quercus, it is not very strong and doesn't last as long as I would like. I want to really smell the cologne and have it linger, but it fades away into nothingness after a few, short, glorious hours.

I haven't worn any of the women's fragrances, but have smelled them on my wife. I enjoyed all of them, particularly Vaara and Ellenisia. Iris Prima, Orange Blossom and Artemisia are all pleasing as well, but those first two really jump out! So far I haven't smelled something from Penhaligon's that I haven't liked and most of them I've LOVED. So glad that I got this "Scent Library" because it really has helped me know which Penhaligon's fragrance I want to purchase next!

title: Comparison of 12 eyeliners
text:
I purchased 12 eyeliners and tested them to see which ones I liked most. I apply my eyeliner to what's known as "the waterline" of the eye, the inside of the bottom eyelid. I wanted an eyeliner that would last all day and would not smear and make me look like a raccoon. I didn't find any that were perfect. The highest rating I gave to any were 4 stars, and there were three that fit that rating. The list is below, from highest rated to my least favorites.

Here are the results:
Eyeliner Test

I rated it: 4 stars
Brand: Superwear
Name: Gel liner
Application: easy
Lasts: fairly well, nearly all day
End of Day: no raccoon look, so as the eyeliner disappears, at least it doesn't smudge

I rated it: 4 stars
Brand: Scandal Eyes
Name: Waterproof Kohl Kajal, Rimmel London
Application: easy
Lasts: no, disappears
End of Day: somewhat of a raccoon look

Brand: Malibu Glitz

End of Day: somewhat of a raccoon look

Brand: Aqua Eyes
