To remove hair from under the comb, you have to slide off the clear plastic comb and length assembly, blow it out, then carefully align and slide it back into the little slots, making sure to set it on the same length setting as before. Had I known they designed it this way, I never would have bought it. The last Norelco I owned had a comb on a pop-up hinge, so it took only a couple of seconds to blow out the hair and continue using it. And I didn't have to worry about the length setting each time I cleaned it. I assumed this product would be the same, but noooooooo! This thing is a pain in the backside by comparison!

One more thing, the clear plastic comb/adjustment has a little "ratchet" on it for the length adjustment, which I think will wear out quickly because of constantly sliding the thing on and off. That is to say, a little piece of plastic which makes a "riiiiiiiip!" sound when sliding it on or off. Oh, and the length indicators are tiny and hard to see. Even though I'm nearsighted (making close-up work easier), I have to look carefully at it each time I slide it back on. Slide it too far, and ruin your beard--WHOOPS!!!

I just learned it will not run plugged-in when the battery is dead. To me this is the last straw. 1-Star!

title: Great medium to full coverage foundation!
text:
I LOVE this foundation. It doesn't get oily during the day, which is a huge plus for me since I have pretty acne-prone skin.
It dries to a nice, almost-matte finish and has very good coverage for being a mineral foundation.

The only qualm I have with this foundation is that it's kind of hard to guess which shade you will be.
I ordered the Linen (I am usually in the Ivory to Nude shade range in other foundations with a warm undertone) and although it matches my neck well, it makes my face look kind of flat. I solve this by mixing in a small amount of a darker shade foundation whenever I apply it and it looks perfect.

During the winter, make sure you moisturize often, as this foundation will eventually show your dry spots since it dries into a powder (every powder foundation I've ever used does this too, so I can't complain too much). During the summer, or if you never get dry skin, this foundation will look flawless.

If you think you're between shades, I would order both and just mix them together into whatever shade you need. This way, if you're tan in summer and pale in winter, you'll be able to use mixes of this foundation year-round.

Even though it's a little pricey (I buy cheap drugstore foundation), I would definitely buy this again as soon as I run out. If you normally buy expensive liquid or mineral foundation, you should give this a try. I think it's the best of both worlds at a much better price.

title: Some potential hazards lead me to believe this product would not be ideal for anyone even if a good color match
text:
Pros:
-- It is similar to other aerosol dry shampoos in being adequate, but not outstanding, in serving the purposes (oil-control and giving fine hair the look of more fullness)

Cons
-- I have come to realize from comparison that a non-aerosol product like Oscar Blandi Pronto Dry Shampoo does a better job of getting at the root area and giving a much denser look to my thin hair (but I am lucky in that I can effectively use a white powder product like Blandi due to my extra light hair color)
-- For me, the "Light" part of the "Light and Blonde" color description was a complete failure as it was way too yellow/golden for my pale blonde/white hair.
-- What knocked it from 3 stars (which I was thinking of giving because the color may suit users with golden hair) to 1 star is that the Environmental Working Group's free "Skin Deep" website (ewg.org/skindeep/) rating system for hazard level of the Batiste Dry Shampoo products shows a red zone hazard for "Ecotoxicology, Allergies/immunotoxicity, Irritation (skin, eyes, or lungs), Miscellaneous, Organ system toxicity (non-reproductive)" of some of its ingredients. Being an aerosol, a relatively large amount of this does go into the air to be breathed in, and so I think this warning has validity that would be hard to write-off as being overly-cautious. From now on I plan to consult ewg.org/skindeep/ before making purchases for hair and cosmetic use.

title: Eh.  Nothing special.
text:
I always wear nail polish as a skin condition makes my nails look funky, so I go through a lot of base and top coats. I got a great deal on the Revlon Quick Dry Base Coat, and I'm glad I didn't pay a lot because it is mediocre.

Some of the pros include easy application (not the curved brush that I prefer, but no huge gaps or stiff bristles at least), an easy-to-grip bottle and brush handle, and viscosity.

Some of the cons include it not drying quickly at all (I have several base coats that are not quick-dry and they actually dry faster than this), it not preventing my nails from peeling or chipping for more than 48 hours at best, and it not preventing staining when red polish is applied over it.

This is not the worst base coat I have ever tried, but when a polish markets itself as a quick-dry formula, I think it should feel fairly dry to the touch within a few minutes, and this feels tacky even after 15+ minutes.

title: Awesome Colors and no problems with drying!
text:
I'll start by saying I am not a nail professional, but rather a Mom to two girls who are crazy over all the nail art people on Instagram and YouTube :)

We were looking for some bright colors to do nail art with, but I knew that I did not want to spend $8+ a bottle on the nicer brands like OPI, Essie, China Glaze, etc. Many of the cheap polishes in the stores look bright, but when you apply them, it takes about 10 coats for them to look even half way decent. The reviews on these polishes seem to be mixed, but they weren't bad, and for the price, I figured it was worth a shot.

We recieved these a few days ago, and the girls instantly wanted to try them with the water marble technique because the colors are so bright and seem like they would work well. We found out that these are really thick, and so they did not work well with the water marble. But, because they are so thick, I instantly knew that they would be great for nail art and for stamping.

So, we tested them out with a simple nail art design (picture below) and they were great! I didn't find that they took any longer to dry than any other polish that is out there, and with two coats (which is what you have to do most of the time anyway), the colors were super vibrant and amazing!

I also haven't found problems with chipping either like a lot of the reviews. We use Sally Hanson UV Top Coat and our nails have held up great!

I give these 4 stars and not 5 because the polish is really thick, and so it is a little challenging to do some finer detail work, and the brush inside each bottle is not my favorite. Would I buy these again, absolutely! Are these my go to brand, probably not. But, for the price, colors and the purpose, they are great!

**In my picture, we used the black, navy blue and regular yellow from this set. The white and silver are not this brand. **

text:
This table is great. I've recently upgraded from a $100 table, and the difference is very noticeable.

My top 5 reasons for recommending this table.
1 - 2 tables in one. The table unhooks it's cables to lay flat for Shiatsu massage. With 3 inches of foam (including 1 inch of memory foam), it could double as a guest bed or travel bed. On my other table I could feel the board when laying on my side. Not so with this one.

5 - customer service. The customer service people are pleasant and willing to take the time to help you personally. I reached out to them and got a live person within 3 minutes or so.

For less than $300, this table might provide the best night's sleep you've ever had

title: Sun-Kissed Look
text:
This is an effective and easy-to-use tanning lotion. Although I am a fair-skinned, freckled person who avoids tanning, only one application – very thinly applied – took the shine off of my pale-white skin and replaced it with en even, light-brown hue. Another application, spaced a couple of days apart, was all I needed to establish a “tan.” Idéal Soleil was extremely effective on my skin. I used it once only, and then very lightly, on my face, without any resulting blemishes or irritation. An unexpected benefit: it evened out blotchy areas.

For me, two applications were enough and lasted almost two weeks. My sense is that areas that have previously been sun exposed darken better than areas that have never seen the sun. For instance, the test patch I did on my stomach didn’t even register whereas the test patch I did on my lower leg was obvious. My experience is a completely anecdotal account, but if you have a history of tanning, you may not need a lot to see a good result. The cream is not greasy, does not streak, and spreads smoothly. For me, the fruity, perfume smell is a nuisance. I don't understand why these products can't be odorless. It's not overwhelming, but it is apparent, and transfers to clothing.

Apply just a dime-sized dollop to your palm, rub hands together, and then apply to skin surface. Maybe a dollop per surface area such as lower leg, then upper leg, forearm, then upper arm and so on. Don’t overdue it. Except for the smell, I am impressed with this “self-tanning milk” cream.

title: Amazing. Lost fuzzy frizz gained curls
text:
I perm my hair to get light spiral curls. My hair is normally straight, fine and thin, and the sides are white-grey while the back is healthy and has a little grey in it. The back keeps its curl definition but the sides tend to frizz up after the perm because of being grey. If I air dry my hair, the sides look good until I either pick it or a little time passes. It won't take long before it gets fuzzy rather than curly.

I've tried everything to keep the fuzzy frizz under control from oils to heavy conditioners. All that did was give me oily frizz! I saw this product the other day so gave it a try. It isn't expensive so was worth a shot. All I can say is "WOW" because the sides now have the same curl definition as the back. Even if I pick it out a bit, it keeps the curl and looks healthy and shiny. I dampened the sides (not much) and rubbed about a nickel size blob on my hands then on the sides (in other words, my hair wasn't wet). I had enough left over that I ran it through the back, too. My hair looks amazing - all curl, no frizz. And the curls are not "crunchy" After my hair dries I lightly run my fingers through my curls go fluff them out and I'm good to go. I love this stuff! So much I came here and ordered 4 more to keep on hand. I never want to run out!

I purchased my dryer at BB&B for 399.00. I have long (2inches below shoulder) naturally wavy/curly very thick hair that I blow dry straight in sections. I have used all types of hair dryers from T3 to Babyliss and was currently using a Chi Air Style Ceramic.
I tried the Dyson dryer for 3 dries (I only wash my hair every 3 to 4 days).
Pros: I really liked the sleek design, the magnetic attachments (love this feature), the 3 heat settings, 4 air settings and cool shot - I tried several different combinations of heat and air flow. It was quite and dried my hair faster than any other dryer I've used. It also did not put as much heat into the room as other dryers.
Cons: The cord was very clunky, the controls were difficult to reach but ultimately - I did not like the texture of my hair during the drying process. It had this dry straw like texture. It eventually calmed after touching it and putting a serum on after drying. And my hair did look good. But did it look $320.00 better than when using my $80.00 Chi? No. For this amount of money, I was expecting a lot and ultimately it just didn't deliver.
So,I returned my dryer.

I would also be very cautious buying this product from Amazon. Some of the sellers are selling refurbished dryers which is where mechanical problems arise.

text:
You get what you pay for! None the less, I knew I wasn't getting a high quality product when I purchased these brushes. However, I ordered them anyway for one reason: it was a cheap way to try out different brush shapes. Bought these in early January and ran them into the ground by late February. Do not expect these to last you or you'll be sorely disappointed. I used most of these brushes every single day for the month and a half I had them. Here are a few notes on ones that stood out to me:

Flat Brush - Hands down, my favorite style brush. It was dense enough to use for a full coverage look with a liquid foundation. However, this was the first to begin shedding. Then eventually it started falling apart. Literally. The brush was shedding, the metal part came off the handle. Into pieces. I posted photos.

Flat Angles Brush - I haven't used this one as much as the flat brush, but you most certainly could still use for the same purpose. I've retired it as a foundation brush and use it with my setting powder. It sheds.

Tapered Brush - Awesome! Love this style as it makes blending my liquid highligher (L.A. Girl Pro Conceal in Creamy Beige) a breeze. This too sheds I'm afraid.

Small Flat Angled Brush - I love this for blending in my green correcting cream (L.A. Girl Pro Conceal Corrector) in areas where I have redness. I could just use my finger BUT this makes the process less messy for me. It sheds but I'm still able to get a good use out of it.

This is a wonderful set for beginners or if you're looking to try out different brush shapes before splurging on name brand brushes.

title: The Colonel X2L, great brush at first, but didn't last a year
text:
I have been wet shaving for forty years and have owned a few brushes in that time. After a few cheap brushes I have purchased premium Super badger brushes for the past thirty years. The good brushes lasted over ten years each and by the time I need to replace them (after the rush becomes thin and floppy) the labels were worn off and the receipts long gone, so every search for a new brush seems to start from scratch. This time I ended up with the Colonel X2L. I wanted something firm but soft and with a bigger knot than the smaller brushes and that is exactly what I got in the Colonel. My choice of Best Badger over Super Badger hair was in the interest of getting a slightly firmer brush. Although it is not as big and tall as some of my other brushes, and I do miss that a bit, the quality is excellent. I have only shaved with it for a week, and it has lost a few bristles, like three or four, good indication of a well made brush. The nice flair on the base of the handle gives me a good grip when I shake the water out of the brush after shaving
Update: After owning the brush for eleven months and using it regularly four days per week it began to lose more and more hairs, until finally I stopped using it altogether. I have always taken good care of the brush and rinsed it and shook out excess water every time I shaved with it. I began to pick out the loose hairs before shaving every morning, but it kept losing hairs as I lathered up, often leaving two or three tickling hairs on my face. When using it went from being a pleasure to unpleasant, I parked it on the shelf. I have attached a picture of the brush showing the number of hairs that fell out every day until I stopped using it.

title: Save a ton on pet grooming at home!
text: The Wahl 9484-300 U-Clip Deluxe Pro is a solid and economical alternative to paying for professional grooming. This kit pays for itself after the first use. As someone who owns a similar clipper designed for human hair (and also made by Wahl), I can tell you that this product is almost identical. All standard Wahl guards fit this model, and it operates no differently than any other. It does have a nice, professional looking design, but despite the claim on the packaging that it stays cool, it most certainly does not. After around 5 minutes of use, it became almost uncomfortable to hold due to the intense heat it generates. This didn't seem to bother the dog (the blades themselves didn't seem to be hot to the touch), but I definitely had to take a few breaks. I'd also like to talk about the strength of the cut compared to the thickness of your dog's fur. I used this to trim a Shih Tzu, which is one of the breeds mentioned on the packaging as a "medium" thickness fur (which the packaging also states the product is designed to handle). The dog in question had not been groomed in several years, so its fur was very thick and curly (even after washing and rigorous brushing) -- the blade couldn't handle it very well with a guard attached. I decided that instead of passing over the same area a hundred times with a guard on, I'd just shave the dog with no guard at all. This worked exceptionally well, and I wish I had just started out this way from the beginning. The bottom line is: If you have a dog with short/straight fur, this clipper will groom your dog with just about any guard and few hassles. If your dog is a little bit on the shaggy/curly side, you're in for a struggle when using the guard. I'm sure that once my little Shih Tzu's fur begins getting longer, it'll be much easier to maintain with a guard on the blade than it was the initial time. Just keep that in mind, and enjoy your otherwise hassle free grooming experience.

title: In depth personal review: "Oster Classic 76" vs "Wahl Elite Pro High Performance Haircut Kit"
text:
I am a non-professional and have been cutting my own hair for about 4 months now. Previously I have been going to a barber a buzz cut (#2 usually or one higher) for about 5 years now & figured I could save some money doing it myself. I started out using the "Wahl Elite Pro High Performance Haircut Kit" which I purchased at a local store. Then I purchased the "Oster Classic 76" on Amazon. This will be a lengthy review but I will give you my in depth personal experience with both and why I switched to the Oster 76.

Wahl Elite Pro High Performance Haircut Kit review:
This is a pretty good kit & I was satisfied for my first couple hair cuts but then I started to notice that it was missing hairs. I thoroughly go over all sections of my head but for some reason it seemed to miss some hairs. Not all that many but it started to get pretty annoying. I would notice them on the sides of my head looking in the mirror for example and would end up getting some scissors to snip them as they were noticeably longer. There really weren't that many so I wasn't too concerned at first. For the life of me, even as a non-professional, I'm not sure why it seemed to miss some after so many passes. This kit was decent as I got it for sub $50 and it came with an entire set of plastic attachable combs. I also have a cowlick that seemed to get left a little longer than the rest of my hair too! I tried cutting it from all directions, using a comb to try to pull back the hair with the clippers following, etc. As I mentioned I am no professional, but I don't think a buzz cut is rocket science either. In addition I found these clippers hard to get close around my ears. I think it's due to the fact that it uses plastic attachable blades (aka combs). They are somewhat bulky attachments and the plastic comb sticks out to the sides of the actual razor because it's a clip on attachment. I think this extra width that's added to the razor by using an attachable plastic comb makes it just that much more difficult to get around the ears closely. I was having to (carefully) go back later and cut around my ears without any guard (comb) on because I wasn't able to get hair closely around my ears with this razor. Which although I have a steady hand, as a non-professional, I prefer to avoid having to cut without any guard on, for obvious reasons. Seeing as this is a kit it also came with some blade oil...but the small blade oil plastic bottle always leaks! This comes with a carrying case to hold everything (which is nice) and if the bottle isn't standing upright it will leak (if on it's side for example) even though it has a screw on cap. At the end of the day these clippers gave me a decent cut but it just wasn't quite as nice as what I received from a barber. However, through using these I decided that I really enjoyed giving myself my own hair cuts and decided to invest in a more quality pair of clippers.

Oster Classic 76 review:
After my experience with the Wahl kit I decided to try investing in a more professional grade pair of clippers and did a decent amount of research on different clipper options before opting for this. I ordered the Oster 76 and a #2 blade (this only comes with a couple really short blades). This clipper by far (personally) gave me a far better hair cut on the first time that I ever got while using the Wahl kit. I didn't notice any of the longer hairs that seemed to get missed with my Wahl razor. In addition, the cowlick that I have on the front of my head that seemed to not get cut well previously cut nicely just like every other portion of my hair with this razor! As I mentioned in my Wahl review, the plastic comb attachments in that kit are what I believe made it more difficult to get around my ears since they are a bulky attachment. To be fair, and as a disclaimer, I did not try metal blade attachments with the Wahl razor (would have to purchase seperate) so they might be more comparable to the Oster blades. I used the #2 replacement blade and I believe having no bulky comb attachment on top of the razor lets me get real close to my ears. I did not even have to go back later and trim around my ears! As I mentioned, I think this is more of the difference between using a metal replacement blade compared to a bulky plastic comb attachment. Like the Wahl kit this comes with some included blade oil. Thankfully, the included blade oil container does not leak! These clippers do not come with a case to store them in though which will be another added expense when I find one, it was nice that the Wahl set had that, but that was more of a "kit" compared to this. A downside to this razor is it's a little expensive, especially if you're purchasing addition blades! The razor itself was over twice as much as the Wahl kit I tried. Then I purchased an additional blade, and plan to purchase one more, plus some extra blade oil, and some wash. It will probably end up running me $200 after tax and everything to get a couple extra blades and accessories, and that's not including a case. So seeing as I paid about $20 for a haircut (once a month) I could see this paying itself off in less than a year. But now that I cut my own hair, I do it every two weeks, so I guess it's definitely getting it's moneys worth.

Conclusion:
Although I've had these clippers for less than a month and have only used them a couple of times I hope that they last a really long time as I have heard many people say they do, but I cannot speak personally for their longevity. Oster has some videos on YouTube which describe maintenance which were helpful. In addition some tips they suggest like attaching the blades while the razor is running(which I wouldn't have thought of). So if you're a non-professional I would suggest looking up a few of their videos. My conclusion would be this: The Wahl clippers gave me a hair cut that was pretty good and for about $40 it's a pretty good bargain for everything it comes with. I knew there was alcohol in them.. but I didn't know it would be THIS much. For all the masks in this pack, the ingredients start with:

Water, Glycerin, Methylpropanediol,, Betaine, Alcohol, 1,2-Hexanediol, PEG-40 Hydrogenated Caster Oil, Xanthan Gum, Salvia Hispanica Seed Extract, Centella Asiatica Extract, Houttuynia Cordata Extract, Sodium Citrate...

There's more, but these are the ingredients that are the same across all the masks; after Sodium Citrate, there's a variation in the ingredients. Alcohol is the 5th ingredient in all the masks, and I'm sure everyone knows that the ingredients in anything bought is listed from greatest to least. Alcohol is pretty high up there (in my opinion). If you don't mind the smell of alcohol, by all means, this is a wonderful deal.. but if you are sensitive to smell or alcohol on your skin, I would pass on buying this if I were you.

title: Works decent - HATE the smell
text:
I'm solidly on the fence about this deodorant. On the upside, it works pretty well. It controls body odor nearly all day and does not mix offensively with it when my natural stink does manage to push through (it's offensive on its own, but I'll get to that later), and it does a decent job controlling wetness as well. I've only noticed damp armpits and odor on the craziest shifts (I work as a waitress) when I'm running around like crazy and stress-sweating. Even then, a quick reapply is all that's needed; on a day of normal activity, I don't have to reapply it. My favorite thing about this deodorant, however, is that, because it doesn't have baking soda (my underarm skin is very sensitive), it doesn't give me a rash or make me itchy at all, which almost all other natural deodorants do. I can even put it on right after shaving and there is still only minimal irritation.

Now for the bad: I HATE the smell. Admittedly, I'm not quite positive what geraniums actually smell like, but I'm pretty sure it ain't this. To me, this smells like rosewater that's gone funky, with maybe a splash of apple cider vinegar added- in other words, NOT what I want to smell like. And it's STRONG, you'll be catching whiffs of it hours after you put it on (I suppose it's better than getting whiffs of rank BO, but only slightly). As other reviews have mentioned, it's very thick and does not go on easily. My biggest problem with it, though, is that it comes off on all my clothes. Thinking of going sleeveless? You can forget about it with this deodorant, and especially so if your shirts are dark.

Bottom line: At 10 bucks a stick, I expect to be wowed by my deodorant, and this one just doesn't cut it.

title: It’s okay. Could be great with minor improvements.
text:
Size as described. Product looks just like it does in the picture. It says JUMBO for a reason.

Please hand wash this before using it. I did and it bled a lot in the water. I can imagine it could stain your pillows.

This bonnet actually stays put, surprisingly. Previously I had been using a scarf which I had to secure with five bobby pins. As an active sleeper sometimes I’d wake up and the scarf would still be on the floor. This bonnet however stays on through the night. It does slip a little further back, maybe half and inch, as I sleep, but it’s not a problem.

I suffer from frequent tension headaches, so I’d know if this was too tight, trust me. It’s not. The band is actually some sort of elastic. It’s grippy, not soft at all. So please don’t put this ON your edges, specially if you have braids causing tension at the same time... that sounds like a recipe for getting snatched.

The material is some satin-type on the outside, while the inside is lined with some sort of mesh-y polyester. There is really no purpose for the lining. The after the first few nights I realized my hair was looking dull and lifeless. Of course this type of fabric sucking the moisture and oils out of your hair defeats the purpose of wearing a bonnet. Ended up flipping the cap over to have the satin on the inside.

I would give this five stars if it did not have the lining as it currently does. Someone should tell the makers of this bonnet that ideally we want the benefits of the satin coming in contact with our hair... not with our pillow... (I might just cut it out, will update review if I do)

Edit: After having this since October, and it's now April 2018, I have some more comments to add to the review. I did end up cutting the lining out, it was very easy. After about four months, the band started to stretch in random places, one side is worn out and the other isn't. As a result the bonnet has started to slip off. It hasn't ended up on the floor yet, but it's not ideal. Also, in hindsight, even though I have very long and very big hair, this may have been a little to large for every day use. My initial idea was for me to wear my hair loose under the bonnet, but the logistics of getting all the hair through the opening was a little too difficult. I have knocked down one star from the review, and I am currently looking for a different bonnet, since this didn't even make it to a year.

title: Worked well!
text: This is a "reef safe" sunscreen. Most sunscreens contain ingredients that harm coral and other marine life, and reefs all around the world are damaged and dying. When our family went to Hawaii we chose this because I hoped if my kids returned in 25 years with their children, they would still find thriving reefs and beautiful snorkeling opportunities.  Since it is reef safe it is 1) does not have as high an SPF as typical, non-reef safe sunscreens 2) does not rub in as easily or completely as regular sunscreen 3) leaves a light white cast to your skin 4) is more expensive than some other sunscreens. For us the environmental benefits are worth the compromises. This bottle lasted for 4 adults for about 7 days. It protected us well and prevented sunburns. Consider a reef safe sunscreen anytime you are swimming in the ocean even when not specifically visiting a coral reef.

title: Glows Bright and Applies Well (Plus Advise for Use)
text:
This stuff is great! Had an idea to make one of my seasonal parties a glow party this year. This stuff is easy to smear on or apply with more precision. Once applied, it dries quickly and leaves a nice smooth texture on the skin, while glowing brightly under black lights. I recommend making sure you have 360 degree black light coverage for the best effect, so there's no direction you can turn where the paint goes dim.

Skin cleanup is very easy! 90% will come off with warm water alone, and you can use soap to easily get it all off. Be careful with clothing and furniture... I've found that the paint will stain whites, but generally comes right out of jeans or colors. If you have a house full of people with glow paint on, COVER YOUR FURNITURE. As long as the paint is dry on the skin, it won't stain furniture. What it will do is rub off on it, leading to hours of cleanup with the black lights turned on. I learned this the hard way and covered couches with canvas paint drop cloths after the first time.

Fun stuff overall, and a little mess is to be expected when you use body paint.

title: Old Formulation was MUCH Better (4 stars); This Product is AWFUL Now!
text:
So my original review is below (and I will leave that intact -- 4 stars). My new review is as follows:

The reformulation of this product is AWFUL, AWFUL, AWFUL (can I write that more? YES!) I will point out that Babo added more cheaper "filler" ingredients and upped the price over the past few months (hmm...). Besides changing the ingredients, they now tout their product as "gluten-free" (this is sunscreen, you're not eating it, kids!), I digress... Anyway, they also removed the "extra" from the sensitive skin note on the front of the tube and I can see why after today...

After running out of my last tube, I opened my new tube (I ordered 2 through subscribe and save; I didn't realize the ingredients list had changed; it's too late to return them now...). The texture is certainly much easier to apply than the old formulation but since I cut the product with aloe (another step but easy-peasy), it was something I could live with. The new texture was watery and runny, you have to shake the tube quite a bit first before you use it (something I hated about other "natural" sunscreens like Avalon Organics). At first I thought I had a bad batch. It smelled different too. Once sufficiently shaken (repeat often, probably before you're done applying it to your face), the texture isn't too bad, but it's definitely "slipperier" than the old formula, and not necessarily in a good way. I guess if spreadability was a deal-breaker for you, as it seems to have been for most users, it might be more appealing now (don't expect a miracle with zinc oxide not being "white" though).

As soon as I applied the sunscreen, my face STUNG and BURNED for 10 minutes; my skin isn't dry FYI, so that wasn't the cause. I had no idea why this was happening, I wondered if I had a bad batch and then I compared the tubes... Ingredients change... Apparently the change in the formula is why they took that "extra" sensitive off the label... So if you do have more particular skin, it's not for you... Whatever they did to it caused me to break out too... I also found it flaked/peeled off more easily than the old recipe, even though it does "blend" more easily.

So all in all... I'm done with Babo. They used to have a decent product but since it's not good any more, I'm going to try to find a new sunscreen that doesn't irritate my delicate facial skin. I loved that the old version didn't irritate my skin or trigger breakouts and I could live with zinc oxide "pallid clown makeup face;" I would take that over pilling, burning, and acne. I want a functional, non-irritating non-nanoparticle, zinc oxide sunscreen and Babo no longer fits the bill, which is a shame since they had a great zinc content.

The Rundown:
-Stinging and acne-- it's not for "extra" sensitive skin anymore!
-Cheaper ingredients, higher price
-Product is messier, has consistency issues (very runny without constant shaking)
-Product doesn't actually stay on your skin anymore, but there are fewer issues with giant white smears...
-High zinc content still a plus
_____________________________________________________________
OLD REVEIW:

I like this product and I will continue to buy it. It might not be for everyone though.

Pros:
-Short, simple, relatively safe ingredients (good for sensitive skin, pregnant women, and people who are concerned about lots of "additives...")
-Good EWG rating
-No fragrance!
-If you're the color of Elmer's glue or chalk-- it will blend right in with your skin tone without a problem!
-Zinc is pretty much the best sunscreen ingredient.

Cons:
-It is really thick
-Goes on really, really white so you will need to blend it. I recommend doing a little bit at a time or mixing it with aloe vera gel to improve spreadability so you can blend it in. Or you could mix it in with a little of your regular moisturizer, just make sure you get good coverage and don't dilute the product too much. Remember why you're wearing sunscreen!
-For people who tan or people with non-[paper]white skin, it will be really visible on your skin tone.
-If you get a little oily or sweaty, it will rub off. Make sure to reapply if you haven't done so for several hours-- this goes for all sunscreens anyway!

title: Great Body Wash
text:
I really like this body wash. I read some complaints about how it doesn't have a strong scent, but that is exactly the point. Unlike most body washes, it doesn't completely douse you with fragrances. Instead, it just adds a hint of its 'sandalwood' scent. I mean, just stop and think about it for a second: you put on your body wash, your shampoo, your shaving cream/soap, deodorant, and maybe some other hygiene products every day including whatever detergent you use for your clothes...those are a lot of different smells, and most of us don't think about whether or not they conflict with each other instead of compliment. This just adds a very small subtle hint instead of conflicting with every other scent you put on your body. I always think of these different things as everyday cologne, in that you want to smell nice/appealing, but you don't want to burnout the nostrils of everyone that passes you. This helped me along those lines. As a disclaimer: I am an office worker in that I don't do a lot of manual labor, I sit at a computer most of the day for my job, so I can't tell you whether or not this will be good enough for that.

I also liked the smell itself as it didn't hit me as too sweet or flowery, but it wasn't exactly 'sandalwood' either. Never the less, it has a slightly musky and appealing scent. Others pointed out that you can find it at Target for a couple bucks cheaper so if you want to check your local Target, go for it. I will say that I am very pleased with this for an everyday body wash.

title: Excellent to maintain red colored and straightened hair
text:
I'm naturally black/dark brown-haired and I've been coloring and straightening my hair for years. I've gone from my natural color to blonde and now to red. I started using this product from the time I changed to red few months back. My hairstylist said this product would both help lock up the red and also protect from the chemical processing. If you're a red head you know what I mean, very tough color to maintain. This product has been tremendously helpful in maintaining my red.

It's a small bottle and I first felt like this is going to be a money drainer for me but it's not. I only use it once every 10 days to two weeks and also every time before I'm about to enhance the red at home. Each time I only apply couple tiny dollops of it so the small bottle lasts about 1.5 months for me. My hairstylist suggested that I leave it on for several hours or even overnight but I've never done that. I keep it on for only 10 minutes and it still does its job. So perhaps it would be even more amazing if I left it on for hours.

The smell is good, not at all over-powering which is what I want because I'd rather my hair smells my shampoo and conditioner. Sometimes though, the product's after-smell can be a tad bit funky, I'm not sure how else to explain it, but that has never deterred from the product working great. The smell doesn't overshadow the shampoo or conditioner's aroma so I can't complain. All in all, I'm very pleased with this tiny bottle and intend to keep using it as part of my hair routine.

title: Quality ingredients yield measurable results
text:
I think that this is a decently made product. The ingredients are quality, and they're present in concentrations that will actually do something. According to a customer service rep whom I emailed, the niacinamide is present in 5%; research shows that it is effective at concentrations between 1-5%. This is awesome because niacinamide stimulates your skin's production of ceramides, natural lipids that are a part of your skin's protective barrier. They also use Magnesium Ascorbyl Palmitate, a form of vitamin C that has been shown to be effective in anti-aging in concentrations above 5%. Lastly, Hyaluronic acid is one of my favorite ingredients because it pulls moisture from deeper layers of skin up to the surface.

After using this serum for a couple months, the dark post-acne spots on my face have faded considerably, though I do attribute some of that progress to cheap ole' time! The serum is a bit tacky after application, which put me off at first because I don't like the feeling of leftover product on my skin. However, I emailed their customer service department and they said--in a very detailed, thoughtful response--that I can rinse off the product once it's dry without sacrificing any efficacy. Apparently the vitamin C absorbs into the skin within seconds and the niacinamide absorbs within a minute, so there's no need to keep it on longer than that.

Note that when the serum arrives it should be a very light, translucent yellow. As it ages, that color will darken due to oxidation. I recommend using up all the product within three months because it will lose efficacy over time.

title: Good product, but Andis seem to have cut costs on the container.
text:
This is the 2nd time I've bought this. The 1st time, I'd have given the product 5 stars without reservation. This time out, I'd give it 3.5 stars, but would err on the side of a lower rating.

The liquid itself is great, and works the same as the 1st time -- that is, it works as expected.

However, Andis seem to have made a bad decision changing their plastic canister. It looks the same, is sized the same, but is definitely not the same. The product I received has a noticeably softer plastic body canister. So soft that it bends when being held to the point that it becomes near impossible to screw on the lid properly. I now practically have it semi-open as the lid is really just a pain to thread properly with the warping canister. The plastic on this one seems to be nowhere near as stiff as it needs to be. No such problems with my first experience with the product a couple of years back.

Relating as well to the seemingly new material for packaging, the foil seal on the canister was also disappointment. It's one of those that was stuck with some adhesive that doesn't come off cleanly. In fact, the mouth of my canister is still lined with the foil that won't come off, much less come off cleanly. It was another annoyance that presented itself from the very start (upon opening, obviously).

Good product, but Andis seem to have cut costs on the container.

title: My skin feels like skin again
text: Just wow!! I'll start by saying right now my skin is pretty broken atm. My moisture barrier is wrecked from over exfoliation (battling acne almost 20 years) and I have early signs of aging and a whole host of issues. On top of that I put a product with petroleum on my skin in hopes of helping heal my skin...but I had a bad reaction that left me with a red itchy rash all over my face. I have tried every kind of moisturizer, expensive and not, and everything burns, left my skin feeling tight and dry, or my skin reacted badly. Then I came upon this in someone's blog and after one use...omg. This is amazing. My poor parched burnt face soaked this up. No burning, no reaction just sweet sweet moisture. I left it on for awhile till i felt my skin had soaked up all it could and, honestly, this was the first time my face had felt like real skin, not dry crepey paper, in 6 years. I could have cried. I sealed with 100% raw shea butter (the only thing I can use lately) and in the morning my skin still felt so happy. This is my first K-beauty experience and I'm in love. I'm going to keep doing it nightly and will update when all 10 are done. If you need some healing and moisture and have sensitive skin prone to breakouts give it a whirl. I hope it works so wonderfully for you.

I also like to put a little over a nude lipstick to give it a little shine, and it keeps my lips from getting dry from a matte lip color. title: The best natural deodorant I've tried! Actually works for me!
text:
Love this deodorant! First, I am not typically a smelly person, even after sweating from running on a hot summer day, BUT when I stress I get B.O. (think public speaking at work or a party, which is the worst time to get B.O. cause I'm surrounded by people!) I've smelt better deodorants, but this has grown on me, it's a very strong cucumber-y smell. I put it on first thing in the morning without a shirt on, then do my morning routine for a few min., and when my armpits are dry I finished getting dressed. Once it is dry, I never smell it, even when I am sweating. This is the first natural deodorant that I've tried that works ALL THE TIME! I have done lots of public speaking with this and have not had B.O. yet!

Toms of Maine: Does not work at all for me! It actually made me smell bad after a little sweat, and even when I didn't sweat. When I had it, it was better for me to not use deodorant and smell "natural", which is what I did.

Crystal deodorant: This deodorant actually did it's job for the most part and was found at my local drug store. If I sweated from stress, I had some B.O. though. I'd have to apply alot in the morning, then bring it to work and apply before events. I'd actually recommend this to people that don't sweat much or have much B.O. If I run out of Kiss My Face, I'd buy Crystal again until I ordered more.

title: Love this cruelty free Kabuki!
text: As someone who is a makeup addict I'm always looking for new brushes to get that flawless makeup application. I am addicted to my makeup brushes just as much as the makeup itself. I just love having awesome brushes. I look at how soft it is, how comfortable it is to hold, if there's any fall out from the makeup product or if any bristles fall out of the brush when being used and being cleaned. As soon as I received this Kabuki brush in the mail I inspected it a bit. It was super soft and the bristles were dense. They packed a lot of bristles in it which is awesome. I washed it right away. Not many bristles fell out during the washing process. Of course, with any brush I've ever had, from a $50 brush to a $5 brush, they have all lost some bristles in this process so it was nothing to worry about. Once dried and ready for use I tested it with my liquid foundation. This Kabuki brush really smoothed out my liquid foundation on my face and gave me a really nice and flawless finish. There were no brush lines on my face and no bristles came out while applying my makeup. (Which I absolutely hate when that happens!) Overall, I think this brush is really nice. It's made of quality materials, it's durable, it's soft, and it really does just look like a nice professional Kabuki brush. Another plus about this brush is that it's cruelty free and NOT tested on animals! That is a HUGE plus in my book. I highly recommend this brush as the price is very reasonable as well. *Sample provided for review and testing.*

When it got here, I started to use it almost immediately and I was kind of freaked out by how much dead skin came off my feet.

It's important to note here, that I'm one of those all summer flip-flips, barefeet all day, super dry skin people. My feet had callouses a quarter inch or half inch deep. They cracked a lot and were painful and ugly. I was ashamed of my feet and my mom was not afraid to let me know my feet looked horrible. Randomly, bits of the callouses would peel off and seriously, there'd still be more callous below. It was horrible.

Well, within a few minutes, my feet went from hideous to super cute. I keep looking at them now to make sure they haven't reverted back to hideous!! It's so weird to feel the edge of my heels which have been calloused for literal years. This product is terrific.

I will post an update if my skin falls apart or something, but so far so GREAT. Also, I took pictures to show the difference, but really my heels before hand are so hideous I haven't posted the before and afters because I don't want to scar people who look at the pics. title: For quick, painless, easy removal of that embarrassing "lady mustache".
text:
You know that thing that happens when you get older? The thing we dare not speak of, or admit to anyone? That thing where we start sprouting coarse facial hair?

Ugh. I know it's natural. People have hair. On their faces. Even women. But why can't it remain fine and light? It's not even dark, just thick and coarse. And then there's that time your toddler nephew runs up to give you a hug and announces to the room that Aunty is growing "whiskers" and the earthy swallowed me whole and I died.

Okay, it wasn't that dramatic.
So I wax. Or thread. Depends on which little salon I can get into. But work gets busy. Or the weather's bad. Or I'm just lazy. And suddenly I realize it's been awhile. And I have a date. Or a client meeting. Or a networking event. And I don't have the hour it'll take to jump on a bus, or walk over to the salon, wait in line, get waxed, get home, get ready. And plucking? That sh*t is painful. You can wax my whole body and I'll fall asleep I'm so relaxed. Tweeze one hair and I'm sobbing in pain. It is what it is.

Enter, these little "eyebrow" shapers. Lifesavers.
The handle is thin, like a longer version of those dental flossers. Topped by a single short razor blade, wrapped with a thin safety wire (similar to what Schick does with their disposable razors). Capped with a clear cap.

Personally I find these totally unsuitable for eyebrows. Maybe just because my eyebrows are thinner and/or the shape I keep, but I couldn't do any of the detail shaping I do with these razors. But they are perfect for lip/chin/face.

You don't need to apply any pressure. Or use any shaving creams. Just lightly skim your face, holding taut the area, and holding the shaper razor at a roughly 45 degree angle. Holding it at a 90 degree angle removes less hair, and may lead to nicks. Yes, even with the safety razor, you can still nick your skin, so be sure not to press down onto your face with it.

title: An expensive optional treatment
text:
Having been a PC customer since the 90's and having combination skin, I've tried, in an effort to keep my oily skin tamed and my dry skin moisturized, every one of PC serums. Because PC uses published reputable skin care research to determine the ingredients, it's hard to argue with the potential benefits of the ingredients in each formulation. So what it truly comes down to is how your skin reacts to the particular ingredients and how well you like the texture and feel. Being the newest antioxidant serum in the line, this one has some intriguing ingredients that the others lack. But the main difference here, for better and worse, is that the product is a watery, near-toner like consistency. Love the silkiness of the silicones in the original PC antioxidant formula? Well if you do, this one will likely disappoint. But if you felt weighed down by the original serum (I think now rebranded as the Resist Serum for dryer skin types), you may find this one a nice change of pace. I find that my skin needs the richer serum in the winter and this one in the summer.

This one, because of its water like texture, would be better off in a pump measured dispenser. It's very easy, especially when the tub is less than half full, to dispense way too much product. And while PC states that this product goes well over skin, I find that it absorbs very fast, perhaps too fast in that you can't get that small amount over the entire face before the product is absorbed. This can be remedied by putting a small drop of this with a couple of pumps of the Resist Clear Skin Hydrator as each of the products assist the other in covering the entire face.

Whether or not you truly need this expensive product if you are already using a nicely formulated toner, exfoliator, moisturizer and over the counter or prescription retinol treatment probably once again depends on whether you are a skin care junky or not. This one is probably an optional but nice step to add. But don't expect the wonderful anti-aging benefits that a prescription retinol or high dose over the counter retinol can give you. Then again, if you are sensitive to retinol, this one might be a very nice step to add if you are concerned with skin aging.

Deciding between this one and the other PC serum (Skin Balancing Serum) designed for oily skin? (Yes PC has WAY too many products!). Well, the original oily skin serum comes out as a much thicker gel but is not nearly as silky smooth as the dry skin PC serums. title: Highly Recommended Quality Aftershave
text:
Great product. Bayberry Coast's products are among the best after shave products a man can buy. Before this my experience with after shaves was the stuff you could get at the supermarket--aqua velva, old spice, brut, skin bracer,--you get the drift. Bayberry Coast helped open up my eyes to the fact that there was a world out there of premium shaving products that for the most part you can only get online here on amazon or in specialty shaving websites. This was my first real brush with high end after shave. The only thing I can compare this to in the world of high end after shaves is Captain's Choice (there are 3 captain's choice aftershave bottles in my cabinet). And although Captain's Choice is a very good quality and I use it, I feel the Bayberry Coast gives you a higher quality experience for the money. First of all Bayberry Coast uses all natural ingredients so it's safe for those with allergies or sensitive skin. There is no artificial coloring or scents here. The ingredients list on the bottle reads simple and clearly--the way it should: Alcohol,glycerin, bay, cinammon, clove, allspice, orange, vanilla, purified water.

Bay Rum scent is a shaving classic--i think all men have at one time or another put on a bay rum aftershave. Bayberry Coast's spin on the classic is a little bit "sweeter" than the classic bay rum we're all used to but it is still readily identifiable as being bay rum. The bottle is classy and definitely looks good behind the shaving mirror in the medicine cabinet. Barberry Coast's bay rum aftershave splashes on "cold." It is definitely a crisp,cool sensation and a sharp scent that wakes you up in the morning. However, despite the fact that the formula has alcohol you don't feel that painful,excessive "sting" that you do with some of the cheaper drug store after shaves. Not only that but it soothes razor burn on contact!! Bayberry Coast made me realize that aftershave doesn't have to hurt in order to work. After you use it it leaves your skin feeling smooth and soft as a baby for hours--it's almost as if you put on some high quality skin cream on your face. It also firms your skin although it doesn't give you that annoying sense of excessive tightness that you can get from some drug store aftershaves (im looking at you skin bracer) as if someone had just injected botox in your face!! This is truly a man's aftershave.

This is definitely meant to be an aftershave first--not a cologne. The Bay Rum scent although pleasant disappears after about 20 minutes or so. This means that if you shave first after waking up, by the time you are ready to walk out the door to get to work you can splash on your favorite daytime cologne and it wont clash with the aftershave. Last, but not least, you get a lot for your money. By saying that i don't just mean the experience of using it, i mean that the physical bottle itself is large. 4 fluid ounces is about the same height as the base of my palm to the middle of my pinky finger. When you open up the bottle you will be pleased to find that it is not a splash bottle with a large opening but rather it has a dropper hole in the middle--ensuring that you cant waste the after shave by accidentally spilling it etc. In order to get a sufficient amount of splash on your face just shake the dropper on your palm--2 or 3 drops should be enough for one side of your face.

If you are on the fence regarding this product then please don't be--buy this aftershave immediately--you wont regret it. I also heartily recommend Bayberry coast's Havana aftershave splash and their Lavender after shave cream.

title: The age and other skin type tests featured in the app are complete BS!!
text:
I wish I could break this review down and give the product two separate reviews...as a facial cleaner I actually do enjoy it. I think the pressure is nice and I like the cleanliness aspect, as the device is very easy to sterilize. It doesn’t get smelly like my Clarisonic do after too many uses. For these aspects alone I would give it a 4 or 5.

I have MAJOR issues with its claims about being able to read your skin and give you an accurate report from the accompanying app. My friend tried it a few days before me and was bummed to report that it told her her skin age was 39...guess what? She is 39, so that wasn’t a major red flag initially. I did find it slightly curious that it guessed her exact age, but I’ve gotten bad at reading other people’s ages, so I just chalked it up to that. I decided to try out my own device. After initially being impressed by the way the cleaning felt, I decided to launch the app and enable the skin testing features of the product. Red flag number one: it asked me my age BEFORE I did anything else. I feel like your actual age should be irrelevant when it is trying to determine the age of your skin based on diagnostics. I honestly answered 39, then I submitted to the variety of tests it threw at me. In the end I was notified that I had skin aged 39. This stuck out to me because now it had accurately guessed the exact age of both my friend’s and my own skin, even though we have vastly different skin types and skincare routines.

The next day I deleted my app profile and reloaded it. This time when it asked me my age I declared that I was a healthy 25. After going through the exact same skin tests using the device as I had the previous day, I was notified that my skin age was in fact 25!
Woohoo! I’m practically ageless!!

Not the complete skepticist, though I had very good reason to be, I deleted the app once more. After all, I was wearing serum and moisturizer today, which I don’t believe I had been the previous day. Maybe these cometic boosters were giving my skin an unfair advantage in the age department. I reinstalled the app right away and began a fresh approach! This “fresh” approach led me to aging myself a few years...say it isn’t so, but I actually told the machine that I was 43 years old. Armed with my 39 year old skin slathered in serum and retinol moisturizer, I once again subjected myself to the rigorous “testing” of this product. 30 seconds later I had my result and my definitive answer as to whether or not this product was BS or not. I was diagnosed with 42 year old skin within 15 minutes of being diagnosed with 25 year old skin!! 😱

Either this product is a complete scam or I keep falling into time holes at the wrong time...bottom line-wash your face with this product, but don’t trust a word this shady bitch says to you when it comes to the youthful appearance of your skin.
